AI.result: Experiments on structured and semi-structured scenes show higher visual fidelity with fewer Gaussian primitives and faster rendering.
AI.conclusion: Subtract-and-refill is an efficient alternative to purely additive hybrid rendering that preserves reconstruction gradients and avoids hard visibility discontinuities.

title: Expanding the Quality-Coverage Frontier with Competitive Flow Matching
comment: 40 pages, 24 figures. Project page: this https URL
summary: Flow matching (FM) generators often face a quality-coverage tradeoff. Inference-time techniques such as classifier-free guidance raise quality, but at the cost of coverage. We hypothesize this limitation stems from a basic property of the objective: an intermediate noisy image could correspond to many clean images, yet the model can only predict a single velocity, at best averaging over the multiple possibilities. To mitigate this, we introduce competition among predictions during training. We achieve this by augmenting the predictor with a randomly drawn low-dimensional conditioning code $z$. For each training example, we sample $K$ values of $z$ to produce $K$ candidate velocities that compete to explain the target, and apply the loss only to the best-matching candidate. This winner-take-all objective allows different modes to shape different predictions, rather than being averaged into a single compromise. Furthermore, this term naturally enables a new form of guidance, auxiliary conditioning scaling, which complements traditional guidance methods. Together, these two guidance mechanisms show that our method substantially improves the quality-coverage frontier. We validate on ImageNet-256, using two different testbeds, SiT and RAEv2. Given less than 3% of the original SiT pretraining compute for post-training, at the 67% Recall point, our method reduces $\mathrm{FD}_{r,6}$ from 19.22 to 5.91. On RAEv2, at the 70% Recall point, it reduces $\mathrm{FD}_{r,6}$ from 16.83 to 3.18.

AI.tldr: Competitive flow matching trains K candidate velocities driven by a random low-dimensional conditioning code and applies the loss only to the best-matching candidate, which improves the quality-coverage frontier of flow matching generators.
AI.motivation: Flow matching predicts a single velocity that can only average over the many clean images consistent with an intermediate noisy image, so inference-time guidance raises quality at the cost of coverage.
AI.method: K values of the conditioning code are sampled per training example to produce competing velocities under a winner-take-all loss, and a new auxiliary conditioning scaling guidance complements classifier-free guidance.
AI.result: On ImageNet-256, at 67% Recall with SiT the FD_r,6 falls from 19.22 to 5.91 using less than 3% of the SiT pretraining compute for post-training, and at 70% Recall on RAEv2 it falls from 16.83 to 3.18.
AI.conclusion: Winner-take-all competition among predictions substantially improves the quality-coverage frontier of flow matching generators.

title: Segment What It Can Draw: Querying a Text-to-Image Generator with Its Own Images for Skin Lesion Segmentation
summary: Skin lesion segmentation without annotated masks requires the target to be specified through other cues. Existing approaches rely on dermoscopy-specific rules, annotation-derived model priors, or user-selected regions. A general text-to-image diffusion transformer offers a text interface to the target, but its concept-word attention is unreliable on dermoscopy images: in the model's attention-output space, the word-derived skin-to-lesion direction is poorly aligned with the direction separating real skin from real lesions. We show that the direction derived from generated healthy-skin and lesion images is substantially better aligned. Based on this finding, we propose GENIQ, a training-free method that constructs initial skin and lesion prototypes from generated images and refines them using the most skin-like and lesion-like patches from unlabelled dermoscopy images. It scores test patches along the refined direction and applies a gated threshold to suppress contextual spill-over around small lesions. Without inference-time annotations or additional models, GENIQ achieves Dice scores of 0.85-0.88 on three dermoscopy test sets. It outperforms zero-shot and word-based attention methods on all three sets, and a hand-designed dermoscopy pipeline in Dice and IoU on two.

AI.tldr: GENIQ is a training-free skin lesion segmentation method that builds skin and lesion prototypes from images generated by a text-to-image diffusion transformer and scores test patches along the refined direction.
AI.motivation: Annotation-free lesion segmentation is hard because concept-word attention in a general text-to-image model is poorly aligned with the real skin-to-lesion direction on dermoscopy images.
AI.method: Initial skin and lesion prototypes come from generated healthy-skin and lesion images and are refined with the most skin-like and lesion-like patches from unlabelled dermoscopy images; test patches are scored along the refined direction with a gated threshold that suppresses spill-over around small lesions.
AI.result: GENIQ achieves Dice of 0.85 to 0.88 on three dermoscopy test sets, outperforming zero-shot and word-based attention methods on all three and a hand-designed dermoscopy pipeline in Dice and IoU on two.
AI.conclusion: Generated images can give a better-aligned target direction than word-derived attention, enabling training-free segmentation without inference-time annotations or additional models.

title: SD-LoRA: Training-Time Structural Distillation into LoRA for Few-Shot Vision-Language Adaptation
summary: Few-shot adaptation of vision-language models must balance two competing goals: learning fine-grained visual distinctions from very limited supervision and preserving the efficiency that makes frozen CLIP-like models attractive for deployment. Existing lightweight adaptation methods, including prompt tuning, LoRA, and cache-based adapters, typically supervise global image embeddings and therefore underuse token-level structure. Conversely, structure-aware methods exploit local evidence but often introduce additional inference-time computation. We propose SD-LoRA, a structural distillation framework that uses token-level graph reasoning only during training and transfers its effects into a lightweight LoRA-adapted CLIP model. During training, a heterogeneous graph teacher models patch-patch, global-local, and visual-text relations over high-resolution ViT tokens. Rather than retaining this graph at test time, SD-LoRA transfers its structural bias into the shared CLIP-LoRA backbone through implicit distillation and Prototype Predictive Alignment, which aligns graph-conditioned representations with support-derived class prototypes. At inference, the graph teacher is discarded; prediction requires only a single CLIP-LoRA forward pass and a cache-based classifier. Across 11 few-shot benchmarks, SD-LoRA improves over a strong CLIP-LoRA baseline by 2.4/1.8/3.0/2.4/2.0 percentage points in the 1/2/4/8/16-shot settings, respectively, without additional graph computation at test time. Results on base-to-novel generalization, cross-dataset transfer, out-of-distribution robustness, and calibration further show that training-time structural supervision improves both accuracy and transfer reliability. Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: SD-LoRA transfers token-level graph structure from a training-only heterogeneous graph teacher into a LoRA-adapted CLIP model, so that inference needs only one CLIP-LoRA forward pass and a cache-based classifier.
AI.motivation: Lightweight few-shot adaptation methods supervise global image embeddings and underuse token-level structure, while structure-aware methods often add inference-time computation.
AI.method: A heterogeneous graph teacher models patch-patch, global-local and visual-text relations over high-resolution ViT tokens during training; implicit distillation and Prototype Predictive Alignment transfer its structural bias into the shared CLIP-LoRA backbone, and the teacher is discarded at test time.
AI.result: Across 11 few-shot benchmarks SD-LoRA improves over a strong CLIP-LoRA baseline by 2.4, 1.8, 3.0, 2.4 and 2.0 points in the 1, 2, 4, 8 and 16-shot settings, with no extra test-time graph computation; base-to-novel, cross-dataset, out-of-distribution and calibration results are also reported.
AI.conclusion: Training-time structural supervision improves both accuracy and transfer reliability without adding inference cost.

title: Wide View Synthesis from Overlapping Perspective Cameras in Autonomous Driving
summary: Multi-perspective-camera systems are widely adopted since they provide broad visual coverage for autonomous driving, motivating the synthesis of a unified wide view from spatially separated observations. In this work, we formulate wide view synthesis (WVS), which aims to synthesize a geometrically consistent wide view at a specified virtual viewpoint from multiple perspective cameras. Unlike conventional image stitching, WVS requires reasoning about 3D geometry and visibility to handle depth-dependent parallax and occlusions arising from spatially separated camera centers. While vanilla 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) enables high-fidelity view synthesis, its reliance on per-scene optimization limits its applicability to driving scenes. Furthermore, WVS introduces additional challenges, *e.g.*, peripheral stretching under perspective projection and photometric inconsistencies across cameras. To address these challenges, we propose **Wide-View Gaussian Splatting (WV-GS)**, a feed-forward Gaussian-splatting framework that synthesizes wide views without per-scene optimization. Specifically, we introduce Piecewise Perspective Rendering (PPR) to mitigate peripheral stretching through local perspective projections sharing a common camera center, and Spatial Affine Photometric Modeling (SAPM) to account for camera-dependent photometric variations during training. We further introduce **WideDrive**, a synthetic benchmark providing dense ground-truth wide views and adapt a LiDAR-projected sparse-reference protocol to real-world datasets. Extensive experiments on multiple datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of WV-GS for WVS. Dataset and code will be publicly released.

AI.tldr: WV-GS is a feed-forward Gaussian splatting framework that synthesizes a geometrically consistent wide view from overlapping perspective cameras for autonomous driving, without per-scene optimization.
AI.motivation: Wide view synthesis must reason about 3D geometry and visibility to handle parallax and occlusion, while vanilla 3DGS relies on per-scene optimization and perspective projection causes peripheral stretching and photometric inconsistency across cameras.
AI.method: Piecewise Perspective Rendering uses local perspective projections sharing a common camera center to reduce peripheral stretching, and Spatial Affine Photometric Modeling accounts for camera-dependent photometric variation during training; the authors also introduce the WideDrive synthetic benchmark and adapt a LiDAR-projected sparse-reference protocol to real datasets.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple datasets are said to demonstrate the effectiveness of WV-GS for wide view synthesis; the abstract gives no quantitative numbers.
AI.conclusion: WV-GS is presented as an effective feed-forward approach to wide view synthesis, with dataset and code to be publicly released.

title: Perceptual Distortion for Overfitted Video Coding: Sliced Matching in Space, Error Alignment in Time
comment: 5 pages, 4 figures; submitted to IEEE ISCAS
summary: Recent works in neural video coding have increasingly been trading off perceptual quality against reconstruction fidelity at a fixed bitrate. Wasserstein Distortion (WD) offers a principled approach to balancing these objectives by relaxing spatial correspondences in feature matching, enabling lightweight overfitted image codecs to compete with computationally intensive generative decoders. Extending vanilla WD to video, however, presents two challenges: its independent Gaussian approximation limits the expressiveness of feature distribution matching, while unconstrained texture resampling across frames introduces temporal inconsistencies. We address these challenges by distinguishing between the correspondences that can be relaxed and those that must be preserved. Spatially, we introduce a local sliced Wasserstein distortion (SWD) that matches empirical feature distributions through one-dimensional optimal transport, capturing cross-channel dependencies without enforcing exact spatial alignment. Temporally, we employ a novel flow residual that constrains coding errors along motion trajectories, preserving temporal consistency without imposing additional reconstruction fidelity constraints. Evaluated on UVG and HEVC Class B with the overfitted codec COOL-CHIC, our framework achieves BD-rate reductions of 9.2% in DISTS and 3.0% in LPIPS relative to frame-wise WD, averaged over test sequences, while lowering tOF by 10.2% at matched rate.

AI.tldr: The paper extends Wasserstein Distortion to overfitted video coding, using a local sliced Wasserstein distortion for spatial matching and a flow residual that constrains coding errors along motion trajectories for temporal consistency.
AI.motivation: Vanilla Wasserstein Distortion uses an independent Gaussian approximation that limits the expressiveness of feature distribution matching, and unconstrained texture resampling across frames introduces temporal inconsistencies.
AI.method: Spatially, a local sliced Wasserstein distortion matches empirical feature distributions through one-dimensional optimal transport without enforcing exact alignment; temporally, a flow residual constrains coding errors along motion trajectories, with the COOL-CHIC overfitted codec as the testbed.
AI.result: On UVG and HEVC Class B, relative to frame-wise Wasserstein Distortion, BD-rate falls by 9.2% in DISTS and 3.0% in LPIPS on average, and tOF is lowered by 10.2% at matched rate.
AI.conclusion: Distinguishing correspondences that can be relaxed from those that must be preserved improves perceptual video coding while maintaining temporal consistency.

title: VINO: Revisiting 3D Representation Learning with Volume Transformers
comment: Project page at: this http URL
summary: Self-supervised learning has given rise to vision foundation models that learn general-purpose image representations transferable across downstream tasks, yet representation learning for 3D scenes has not achieved comparable success. Motivated by this, we identify key limitations of current 3D representation learning approaches and revisit their core design choices. We first replace the commonly used hierarchical PTv3 backbone with the Volume Transformer, a ViT-like architecture for 3D scenes. We then redesign two core objectives of modern approaches built around student-teacher networks: matching representations across views and predicting masked content from visible context. For the first objective, we separate the roles of teacher and student: the teacher provides clean, consistent targets while the student learns invariance to stronger perturbations. For the second objective, we prevent the student from accessing the masked geometry and instead require it to infer missing representations from visible context only. Finally, we redesign 2D-to-3D knowledge distillation, replacing direct regression of view-dependent image features with view-consistent supervision. Together, these changes form VINO, a framework that learns semantic representations of 3D scenes without labels. VINO substantially improves dense linear probing across indoor and outdoor benchmarks and transfers strongly to out-of-domain settings.

AI.tldr: VINO is a label-free 3D scene representation framework built on a Volume Transformer that replaces the hierarchical PTv3 backbone and redesigns teacher-student matching, masked prediction and 2D-to-3D distillation.
AI.motivation: Representation learning for 3D scenes has not matched the success of vision foundation models, and the core design choices of current student-teacher approaches for 3D are limited.
AI.method: The Volume Transformer replaces PTv3; the teacher provides clean targets while the student learns invariance to stronger perturbations; the student infers masked representations from visible context only; and distillation uses view-consistent supervision instead of regressing view-dependent image features.
AI.result: VINO substantially improves dense linear probing across indoor and outdoor benchmarks and transfers strongly to out-of-domain settings; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Revisiting the core design choices yields label-free semantic representations of 3D scenes that transfer well.

title: MammoSeek: A Mammography Agent with selective zooming for grounded reports
summary: Radiologists read a screening mammogram by first forming a global impression of the four views and then selectively magnifying suspicious regions before assigning a BI-RADS assessment. MLLMs, in contrast, see the whole image at a fixed, reduced resolution, which makes sub-millimeter calcifications invisible, and they perform close to chance on mammography. Therefore, we present MammoSeek, a mammography agent that reproduces this reading process. After forming an impression of each breast, the agent performs selective zooming: it decides by itself which detector candidates deserve a closer look and inspects only those on full-resolution views. Guided by a BI-RADS assessment skill, it then assigns a category and generates a localized, lexicon-structured report for each breast; its assessment is combined with image-model scores in a decision layer to decide recall. On an internal (EMBED) and an external (VinDr-Mammo) dataset, \ours reaches exam-level AUCs of 0.824 and 0.818, far above other MLLMs, mammography agent and CNN classifiers. Selective zooming also outperforms both no zooming and forced zooming in localization, structured-report F1 and recall decisions at low cost.

AI.tldr: MammoSeek is a mammography agent that mimics radiologist reading by selectively zooming into detector candidates on full-resolution views, then assigning a BI-RADS category and a localized structured report for each breast.
AI.motivation: MLLMs see the whole mammogram at a fixed, reduced resolution, which makes sub-millimeter calcifications invisible, and they perform close to chance on mammography.
AI.method: After forming an impression of each breast, the agent decides which detector candidates merit a closer look, is guided by a BI-RADS assessment skill, and combines its assessment with image-model scores in a decision layer to decide recall.
AI.result: Exam-level AUCs are 0.824 on the internal EMBED dataset and 0.818 on the external VinDr-Mammo dataset, far above other MLLMs, a mammography agent and CNN classifiers; selective zooming outperforms both no zooming and forced zooming in localization, structured-report F1 and recall decisions.
AI.conclusion: Selective zooming at low cost lets an agent reproduce radiologist-style reading and outperform whole-image MLLMs and CNN classifiers on mammography.

title: Householder Motion Embedding: Noise Modulation for Motion-Controllable Video Generation
summary: Diffusion models for video generation have achieved remarkable success, yet precise motion control under explicit user guidance remains challenging. Recent noise-warping methods introduce temporal correlations by warping the noise according to the user-provided motion signal. However, standard spatial warping generally disrupts the noise's i.i.d. Gaussian structure, requiring distribution correction, such as Jacobian-based correction, but at a substantial computational overhead. We propose Householder Motion Embedding (HME), which encodes the motion signal into the noise through a sequence of Householder reflections that together form an orthogonal transformation applied to each location's channel vector. HME exactly preserves the spatial Gaussian structure within each frame while introducing cross-frame correlations that promote temporally consistent video. HME is agnostic to the network architecture and integrates directly into standard video diffusion fine-tuning pipelines. Experiments on different scenarios show that HME matches or outperforms the state of the art, while achieving a 2.7x speedup over noise warping. These results demonstrate that channel-space Householder transformations offer a principled and efficient alternative to noise warping for motion-controllable video generation.

AI.tldr: Householder Motion Embedding encodes motion into video diffusion noise through Householder reflections, preserving the per-frame Gaussian structure while adding cross-frame correlations for motion-controllable video generation.
AI.motivation: Noise-warping methods disrupt the i.i.d. Gaussian structure of the noise under spatial warping, which requires costly distribution correction such as Jacobian-based correction.
AI.method: The motion signal is encoded as a sequence of Householder reflections that together form an orthogonal transformation applied to each location's channel vector; the method is architecture-agnostic and integrates into standard video diffusion fine-tuning.
AI.result: HME matches or outperforms the state of the art across different scenarios and achieves a 2.7x speedup over noise warping.
AI.conclusion: Channel-space Householder transformations are a principled and efficient alternative to noise warping for motion-controllable video generation.

title: ArtiVidRM: Verifiable Artifact-as-Rubric Reward Modeling for Explicit Quality Articulation in Video Generation
summary: Reinforcement learning has become an effective approach for improving video generation, but its success depends heavily on reliable reward models. Existing methods either map videos directly to opaque scalar scores or generate free-form rationales that are not explicitly optimized as the basis of the final judgment. We propose ArtiVidRM, a verifiable, artifact-as-rubrics video reward model that follows an observe-then-score paradigm. It first identifies visible generation artifacts and organizes them into a structured artifact list, then uses these artifacts as explicit rubrics for quality assessment. This intermediate representation grounds each score in concrete video-level evidence, making the reward more interpretable and informative for optimization. We further introduce a multi-reward reinforcement learning strategy to jointly optimize artifact prediction and quality assessment. The reward decomposes into complementary objectives that evaluate artifact prediction quality, including semantic coverage and prediction efficiency, together with a pairwise preference objective that supervises quality ranking through score differences. By jointly optimizing the intermediate artifact representation and the downstream preference prediction, the model learns to produce informative artifact lists while improving the accuracy of video quality assessment. Experiments show that ArtiVidRM achieves state-of-the-art performance on video preference benchmarks, provides effective signals for video diffusion optimization, and enables artifact-guided refinement of closed-source video generators.

AI.tldr: ArtiVidRM is a video reward model that first lists visible generation artifacts and uses them as explicit rubrics for quality scoring, trained with multi-reward reinforcement learning.
AI.motivation: Existing video reward models output opaque scalar scores or free-form rationales that are not explicitly optimized as the basis of the final judgment.
AI.method: An observe-then-score paradigm organizes identified artifacts into a structured list used as rubrics; a multi-reward reinforcement learning strategy jointly optimizes artifact prediction (semantic coverage and prediction efficiency) and a pairwise preference objective based on score differences.
AI.result: ArtiVidRM achieves state-of-the-art performance on video preference benchmarks, provides effective signals for video diffusion optimization, and enables artifact-guided refinement of closed-source video generators.
AI.conclusion: Grounding scores in explicit video-level artifact evidence makes the reward more interpretable and more useful for optimization.

title: Where Do Reported Long-Video QA Gains Come From? A Controlled Audit of Frame Selection, Evidence Injection, and Expert Routing
summary: Long-video question answering is usually studied as frame selection: which few frames should a vision-language model see? We introduce VideoRouteAudit, a controlled audit that separates this choice from two alternatives, injecting non-visual evidence and routing to another answering model. It holds the backbone, frame budget, decoding, prompt and grader fixed while varying one decision at a time. On the full Video-MME long bucket (n=900, K=8), no tested selector significantly improves over uniform sampling. The largest selection-only estimate is +1.9 pt (95% CI [-1.2,+5.0]) and our cascade is +1.2 pt [-1.7,+4.1]; all are equivalent to uniform within +/-5 pt. The same contrasts are unstable at the n=200 subset scale commonly used: three of four are up to 3.8x larger, one reverses sign, and resampled 200-item subsets reverse the full-bucket effect's sign in 35.8% of draws. The audit also corrects our own first results. The anomaly-domain "+ASR" arms injected no text, so the pooled +4.7 pt gain was selection plus a development prefix. With transcripts, ASR lowers XD-Violence accuracy by 10.0 pt when appended after the question and not at all when placed before it, and lowers UCF-Crime by 13.0 pt either way; on Video-MME, placing it first adds about 4 pt (7 on Qwen2-VL) to uniform sampling and to the cascade alike (post hoc, unadjusted). Swapping the answering model gives the largest contrast (+15.1 pt on MUSIC-AVQA, +33.3 pt on its worst type), but the same audio-visual expert with its soundtrack silenced keeps 92% of the gain (69% with a mismatched soundtrack), so the contrast is mostly a model swap. Code, per-item predictions and scripts that recompute every statistic are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: VideoRouteAudit is a controlled audit of long-video QA that separates frame selection from injecting non-visual evidence and routing to another answering model, finding that most reported gains are small, unstable or driven by the model swap.
AI.motivation: Long-video QA is usually studied as frame selection, but reported gains can come from confounds such as injected text, prompt prefixes and changes of answering model, and commonly used small subsets are unstable.
AI.method: The audit holds backbone, frame budget, decoding, prompt and grader fixed while varying one decision at a time, evaluating on the full Video-MME long bucket (n=900, K=8) and on subsets, with ASR transcripts placed before or after the question and an audio-visual expert with its soundtrack silenced.
AI.result: No tested selector significantly improves over uniform sampling; the largest selection-only estimate is +1.9 pt (95% CI [-1.2, +5.0]) and the cascade is +1.2 pt; resampled 200-item subsets reverse the full-bucket sign in 35.8% of draws; ASR appended after the question lowers XD-Violence accuracy by 10.0 pt and UCF-Crime by 13.0 pt; swapping the answering model gives +15.1 pt on MUSIC-AVQA, of which 92% remains with the soundtrack silenced.
AI.conclusion: Reported long-video QA gains are often insensitive to selection or confounded, and the largest contrast in the audit is mostly a model swap.

title: MIKU: Material Invariance and Knowledge Unification for PBR Generation
comment: The Project Page is: this https URL. The Paper is published in SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 (TOG)
summary: High-quality material generation for physically based rendering (PBR) remains challenging because datasets and synthesis pipelines lack standardized representations. Differences in material definitions, rendering conventions, and parameterizations lead to unstable and physically implausible results. We propose MIKU, a unified framework for standardized PBR asset representation and physically consistent material generation across diverse 3D content domains. Its core is a unified processing pipeline that standardizes the workflow from data preprocessing to final texture synthesis, maintaining consistent geometry and texture representations. A normalization scheme harmonizes heterogeneous material parameterizations in a common representation space, enabling robust cross-dataset training and inference. Building on this formulation, we train a novel physically aware diffusion model for PBR texture generation within a two-stage multi-view synthesis framework. First, geometry-aware albedo generation synthesizes multi-view albedo maps under explicit geometric guidance to ensure cross-view appearance consistency. Second, metallic-roughness generation uses the diffusion model to predict physically plausible roughness and metallic maps conditioned on the generated albedo and unified representation. Trained end-to-end on standardized data, the model learns to generate materials that respect category-level material priors and semantic part boundaries. By decoupling representation standardization from appearance synthesis, MIKU substantially improves material generation stability and physical consistency. Extensive experiments demonstrate state-of-the-art texture quality and semantic consistency across object parts, advancing automated material generation for 3D content creation.

AI.tldr: MIKU standardizes PBR asset representation across heterogeneous datasets and uses a two-stage multi-view diffusion pipeline that generates albedo first and then physically plausible metallic-roughness maps.
AI.motivation: Material generation for physically based rendering is unstable because datasets and synthesis pipelines use inconsistent material definitions, rendering conventions and parameterizations.
AI.method: A unified processing pipeline and a normalization scheme harmonize heterogeneous material parameterizations in a common representation space; geometry-aware albedo generation synthesizes multi-view albedo under explicit geometric guidance, then metallic-roughness generation predicts maps conditioned on the albedo and the unified representation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments are said to show state-of-the-art texture quality and semantic consistency across object parts; the abstract reports no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling representation standardization from appearance synthesis substantially improves the stability and physical consistency of automated material generation.

title: WeLM-Image: A Unified Image Generation Model towards Visual Intelligence
summary: We present \textbf{WeLM-Image}, a unified image foundation model that integrates multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and multi-reference synthesis. Designed for single-GPU deployment in WeChat's large-scale consumer applications, the model processes text, reference images, and target latents as one interleaved sequence. A Mixture-of-Transformers (MoT) backbone combines shared attention with independent understanding and generation parameters to limit optimization interference. Equipping each path with Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) modules provides sparse capacity, with 31.7B stored parameters and approximately 5.4B generation parameters activated per target latent token. A generation-oriented data engine combines a knowledge-grounded visual vocabulary with large-scale visual clustering to balance semantic coverage and editing tasks, while training-time evaluation guides iterative data refinement. Bilingual annotations and verified editing supervision support progressive training up to native 1.5K resolution. We optimize generation and editing separately with rubric- and checklist-based rewards, then consolidate the specialized policies through noise-aware on-policy distillation. In the reported overall comparisons, the 1536-resolution model ranks first among the evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench, and UnicBench. MeanFlow-based few-step distillation yields WeLM-Image-Turbo, which generates a $1024\times1024$ image in 4.98\,s on a single NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight guidance-free steps.

AI.tldr: WeLM-Image is a unified image foundation model for text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing and multi-reference synthesis, designed for single-GPU deployment, with a few-step Turbo variant.
AI.motivation: The work aims to integrate multimodal understanding into text-to-image generation for large-scale consumer applications in WeChat, under single-GPU deployment constraints.
AI.method: Text, reference images and target latents form one interleaved sequence processed by a Mixture-of-Transformers backbone with shared attention and separate understanding and generation parameters, with MoE modules giving 31.7B stored and about 5.4B activated generation parameters per target latent token; a data engine, bilingual annotations, rubric- and checklist-based rewards and noise-aware on-policy distillation are used, and MeanFlow distillation yields the Turbo model.
AI.result: In the reported overall comparisons the 1536-resolution model ranks first among evaluated open-source models on PRISM-Bench, Qwen-Image-Bench and UnicBench; WeLM-Image-Turbo generates a 1024x1024 image in 4.98 s on one NVIDIA H20 GPU using eight guidance-free steps.
AI.conclusion: The model combines strong open-source generation and editing quality with practical single-GPU latency.

title: Vis2State: Visual Reasoning through Executable State Abstractions
summary: Solving visual puzzles requires both accurate interpretation of visual evidence and reliable computation under task-specific rules. Embedding visual assumptions and task constraints directly in solving code makes the represented problem difficult to inspect and revise independently. We introduce Vis2State, a training-free agentic framework that abstracts visual puzzles into explicit, revisable problem states linking visual inspection and execution. Visual inspection guides state construction and refinement, while generated programs solve the represented problem. The model constructs both the state and the program without predefined puzzle schemas or solving procedures. Inspection and execution feedback allow it to revise the problem representation and solving procedure independently. Vis2State achieves the state-of-the-art performance on four benchmarks. Cross-model evaluation further demonstrates consistent gains. Ablations, error analyses, and fixed-program state interventions further support the effectiveness of the state-centered design. The code will be made publicly available to facilitate future research.

AI.tldr: Vis2State is a training-free agentic framework that abstracts visual puzzles into explicit, revisable problem states, with generated programs solving the represented problem.
AI.motivation: Embedding visual assumptions and task constraints directly in solving code makes the represented problem difficult to inspect and revise independently.
AI.method: Visual inspection guides state construction and refinement while generated programs solve the state, and inspection and execution feedback revise the representation and the solving procedure independently, without predefined puzzle schemas.
AI.result: Vis2State achieves state-of-the-art performance on four benchmarks and shows consistent gains in cross-model evaluation; ablations, error analyses and fixed-program state interventions support the state-centered design.
AI.conclusion: Explicit, revisable problem states are an effective way to combine visual interpretation and computation for visual reasoning.

title: FreePath: Neural Mean Free Path for Image Dehazing
summary: Single image dehazing requires recovering scene radiance from visual responses that are weakened and veiled by participating media. Existing methods either invert explicit scattering variables, which can be unstable under complex scenes, or learn direct restoration mappings, which often discard the physical organization of haze formation. We present \emph{FreePath}, a neural mean free path framework for image dehazing. Instead of estimating atmospheric parameters, FreePath represents dehazing as feature space path state restoration, inspired by the expected distance a visual response can propagate before interacting with haze. Within a residual encoder and decoder, the Mean Free Path Residual Block learns path and collision fields to guide haze constrained correction, while FreePath State Conservation Integration preserves restored path states during deep feature aggregation. Experiments on paired CDD-11 haze images and real RTTS scenes show that FreePath consistently improves full reference fidelity, no reference perceptual quality, and visual faithfulness over representative dehazing baselines.

AI.tldr: FreePath is a single-image dehazing network that frames restoration as feature-space path state recovery, using learned mean free path and collision fields instead of estimating atmospheric scattering parameters.
AI.motivation: Explicit inversion of scattering variables can be unstable in complex scenes, while direct restoration mappings often discard the physical organization of haze formation.
AI.method: A residual encoder-decoder with a Mean Free Path Residual Block that learns path and collision fields to guide haze-constrained correction, and a FreePath State Conservation Integration that preserves restored path states during deep feature aggregation.
AI.result: On paired CDD-11 haze images and real RTTS scenes, FreePath consistently improves full-reference fidelity, no-reference perceptual quality and visual faithfulness over representative dehazing baselines.
AI.conclusion: Modelling the physical organization of haze in feature space gives a more faithful dehazing alternative to both parameter estimation and direct mapping.

title: PSGAgent: Enhancing MLLMs' Dynamic Visual Perception for Panoptic Scene Graph Generation via Agentic Reasoning
comment: Accepted by ACM Multimedia 2026. 10 pages, 8 figures
summary: Panoptic Scene Graph generation (PSG) requires holistic yet fine-grained reasoning over complex relations among objects. However, current Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) applied to PSG suffer from a perception bottleneck: they function as static observers limited by fixed-resolution views. As a result, models often overlook critical relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes. To address these limitations, we propose PSGAgent, an agentic framework that enhances visual perception for PSG through a think-act-observe loop. PSGAgent allows MLLMs to dynamically refine their visual perception using two tools: a Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration of small or boundary relations and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation that filters out irrelevant contextual noise. To optimize decision-making, we construct a two-stage training pipeline. First, we create a high-quality, error-aware Multimodal Chain-of-Thought (M-CoT) dataset that provides robust supervision for cold-start learning. Then, we design a novel hierarchical reward mechanism integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO) to enable strategic and adaptive tool usage. Extensive experiments on the PSG benchmark show that PSGAgent achieves SOTA performance, demonstrating strong capability in both holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.

AI.tldr: PSGAgent is an agentic MLLM framework for panoptic scene graph generation that refines its perception through a think-act-observe loop with zoom-in and highlight tools, trained with a cold-start chain-of-thought dataset and hierarchical-reward GSPO.
AI.motivation: Current MLLMs act as static observers with fixed-resolution views, so they miss relations involving small or peripheral objects and struggle to differentiate ambiguous predicates in complex scenes.
AI.method: A Region Zoom-In Tool for local exploration and a Visual Highlight Tool for relation-focused segmentation are used in a think-act-observe loop; training first uses an error-aware multimodal chain-of-thought dataset for cold-start learning, then a hierarchical reward integrated with Group Sequence Policy Optimization (GSPO).
AI.result: PSGAgent achieves state-of-the-art performance on the PSG benchmark, with strong holistic and fine-grained scene understanding.
AI.conclusion: Dynamic, tool-based refinement of visual perception improves MLLM-based panoptic scene graph generation.

title: TRiST: Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer for Medical Image Analysis
summary: Medical images contain topological patterns, such as connected components and loops, at scales ranging from small lesions to organ boundaries. Although hierarchical Vision Transformers have advanced medical image analysis, they do not explicitly incorporate topology throughout their multiscale representations. We propose Topology-Reinforced Swin Transformer (TRiST), a framework that integrates topological information into feature construction, refinement, and attention. First, a Hierarchical Multi-Scale Topology Representation algorithm computes 2D persistent homology (H0 and H1) independently at four native Swin stages, producing descriptors aligned with each stage's token grid rather than downsampling fine-scale topology. Second, a Band-Aware H0/H1 Residual Refinement module uses gated residual networks to process short-, medium-, and long-persistence information separately. Third, a Persistence-Band Progressive Attention Bias converts stage-specific descriptors into learned key-saliency scores that directly modify shifted-window attention logits. We instantiate TRiST as Topo-SwinV2-B for classification and Topo-Swin-UNet for segmentation, preserving the underlying Swin-based backbones. Experiments on five medical image datasets show consistent improvements over Swin-based baselines and competitive performance relative to existing topology-augmented methods.

AI.tldr: TRiST integrates persistent-homology topology at four Swin stages into feature construction, residual refinement and attention bias, yielding Topo-SwinV2-B for classification and Topo-Swin-UNet for segmentation.
AI.motivation: Hierarchical vision transformers do not explicitly incorporate topological patterns such as connected components and loops throughout their multiscale representations.
AI.method: 2D persistent homology (H0 and H1) is computed independently at four native Swin stages; a band-aware H0/H1 residual refinement processes short-, medium- and long-persistence information separately; and a persistence-band progressive attention bias converts the descriptors into key-saliency scores that modify shifted-window attention logits.
AI.result: Consistent improvements over Swin-based baselines on five medical image datasets, and competitive performance relative to existing topology-augmented methods.
AI.conclusion: Topology-aware descriptors integrated at multiple stages improve Swin-based medical image analysis while preserving the underlying backbones.

title: VIPA: View-Invariant Projector-Based Adversarial Attack
summary: Projector-based adversarial attack aims to physically manipulate real-world scenes by projecting adversarial patterns, thereby causing deep image classifiers to produce incorrect predictions. However, existing stealthy projector-based adversarial attack methods model the project-and-capture process in a single and static view, limiting their view-invariant capability and practical applicability in dynamic environments. In this paper, we introduce View-Invariant Projector-Based Adversarial Attack (VIPA), a novel method designed to overcome these limitations by achieving both view-invariant and classifier-agnostic adversarial attacks in the physical world. We first leverage a view-invariant projector-camera system simulation method to model the physical interactions between projected patterns and real-world surfaces. To ensure robustness and stealthiness of the attack across different views, VIPA optimizes adversarial projections by aggregating simulated attack losses from multiple views. This joint optimization across diverse views helps maintain robustness regardless of the viewpoints. Finally, the optimized patterns are physically projected into real-world scenes, where they successfully fool various classifiers from different viewpoints, thereby enabling robust and practical view-invariant adversarial attacks. Our experiments in both targeted and untargeted attacks demonstrate that VIPA consistently achieves higher attack success rates than existing methods, while also enhancing stealthiness and ensuring minimal perceptual degradation across all tested views.

AI.tldr: VIPA is a projector-based adversarial attack that optimises projected patterns over multiple viewpoints so they fool image classifiers from different views in the physical world. In targeted and untargeted attacks it reports higher attack success rates than existing methods.
AI.motivation: Existing stealthy projector-based attacks model the project-and-capture process in a single static view, which limits view invariance and practical use in dynamic environments.
AI.method: A view-invariant projector-camera system simulation models the interaction between projected patterns and real surfaces; adversarial projections are optimised by aggregating simulated attack losses across multiple views, and the optimised patterns are then projected into real scenes.
AI.result: In targeted and untargeted attacks VIPA consistently achieves higher attack success rates than existing methods, with better stealthiness and minimal perceptual degradation across all tested views, and it fools various classifiers from different viewpoints.
AI.conclusion: Joint optimisation over diverse views gives robust, practical view-invariant physical adversarial attacks.

title: Compact Motion Embeddings for Feed-forward Unified Human Animation
summary: Animating a reference image with a driver's motion requires a motion representation that captures face, hand, and body articulation but excludes the driver's appearance. Most body animation methods take motion from external pose estimators and render it with many denoising steps; compact learned motion representations mostly cover the face. We present FUHA, a real-time-capable feed-forward transformer that learns a compact motion embedding of the whole human and uses it for face, upper-body, and full-body animation. A Q-Former compresses the driver's features from a frozen visual encoder into this embedding. To disentangle motion from appearance, a novel contrastive loss pulls it toward the motion embedding of the driver's rendered keypoint image and away from that of the same person in another pose. At inference time, FUHA needs no external pose estimators, keypoints, or parametric body models. As a retrieval key, the motion embedding matches body pose better than the learned global embeddings of ten vision encoders. Its same-person retrieval rate is 0.1%, against 9.5% for its own DINOv3 backbone. On our upper-body benchmark, FUHA outperforms all baselines on every self-reenactment metric and on cross-reenactment identity similarity. It is competitive on face and full-body and runs at up to 38.9 FPS at 512x512 on a single RTX 4090.

AI.tldr: FUHA is a real-time-capable feed-forward transformer that learns a compact whole-body motion embedding and uses it to animate a reference image with face, upper-body or full-body motion, without external pose estimators. It outperforms all baselines on upper-body self-reenactment and cross-reenactment identity similarity.
AI.motivation: Body animation methods usually take motion from external pose estimators and render it with many denoising steps, while compact learned motion representations mostly cover only the face.
AI.method: A Q-Former compresses the driver's features from a frozen visual encoder into a motion embedding; a contrastive loss pulls it toward the motion embedding of the driver's rendered keypoint image and away from that of the same person in another pose, which disentangles motion from appearance.
AI.result: As a retrieval key the embedding matches body pose better than the learned global embeddings of ten vision encoders, with a same-person retrieval rate of 0.1% against 9.5% for its own DINOv3 backbone; it is competitive on face and full-body and runs at up to 38.9 FPS at 512x512 on a single RTX 4090.
AI.conclusion: A compact, feed-forward, whole-human motion embedding can drive face, upper-body and full-body animation in real time.

title: Degree-Equalized View-Graph Selection under Tight Pair Budgets
summary: Fully matching all image pairs in Structure-from-Motion is quadratic in the number of images, so practical pipelines pass a budgeted subset to the final matching and reconstruction backend. One-shot selectors score candidates with image retrieval, cheap geometric probes, or a learned prior and finalize B pairs before full matching. Their priorities do not account for the degree already allocated to each image, which can concentrate edges on a few images. Across nine large 1DSfM internet photo collections at B=2N, the coverage top-B selector leaves 54% of covered images with realized degree at most two. Reconstruction can then fail even when the selected graph is nearly connected and almost fully verified. Our training-free greedy rule, Degree-Equalized Allocation (DEAL), exponentially downweights pairs whose endpoints are already well covered. On these collections, DEAL improves the one-shot selector built on the same prior (from 0.776 to 0.929) and matches the mean registered-image ratio of an SfM-supervised edge prior under the shared backend (0.929 vs 0.930), without training. On the largely saturated 38-scene standard benchmark suite, DEAL gives the highest mean among the evaluated training-free selectors (0.875 vs 0.858 one-shot).

AI.tldr: DEAL is a training-free greedy rule for choosing the budgeted set of image pairs for Structure-from-Motion matching; it exponentially downweights pairs whose endpoints are already well covered. It improves a one-shot selector and matches an SfM-supervised edge prior on large internet photo collections.
AI.motivation: One-shot pair selectors ignore the degree already allocated to each image, so edges concentrate on a few images; on nine 1DSfM collections at B=2N the coverage top-B selector leaves 54% of covered images with realized degree at most two, and reconstruction can fail even when the graph is nearly connected.
AI.method: Degree-Equalized Allocation (DEAL) selects pairs greedily under the pair budget, exponentially downweighting pairs whose endpoints already have high allocated degree; it needs no training.
AI.result: On the nine large 1DSfM collections DEAL raises the one-shot selector built on the same prior from 0.776 to 0.929 and matches the mean registered-image ratio of an SfM-supervised edge prior under the shared backend (0.929 vs 0.930); on the 38-scene standard benchmark it gives the highest mean among the evaluated training-free selectors (0.875 vs 0.858 one-shot).
AI.conclusion: Degree-aware allocation is a simple, training-free fix for edge concentration in budgeted SfM pair selection, reaching the performance of a trained prior on large collections.

title: Concertina: Embodying Manipulation and Cognition in One Diffusion Vision-Language Model
summary: Most vision-language-action (VLA) policies decouple manipulation from cognition by bolting an external action mechanism onto a vision-language model (VLM)--either quantizing actions into discrete tokens whose errors bear no stable correspondence to physical displacements, or delegating continuous trajectory generation to a separate action expert whose gradients compete with or are blocked from updating the VLM backbone. We argue that manipulation and cognition should instead be embodied in the same model, shifting from a decoupled VLA to an Embodied Vision-Language Model (eVLM). We introduce Concertina, an eVLM that places continuous trajectory representation, blockwise generation, and physical-coordinate supervision directly on the computation and parameter path of a shared diffusion VLM backbone. Each control timestep is encoded as one continuous latent action token in the backbone hidden space, and the shared Transformer reconstructs temporally ordered action blocks via the same corrupt-and-reconstruct operator used for multimodal pretraining. Active action projections account for only 0.21% of parameters in the 4.46B model with zero separate action-generator layers, compared with 16.5%-35.1% dedicated action-expert capacity in representative continuous VLAs. Using our proposed Action Interface Audit, we confirm that cross-time trajectory coupling emerges in the middle and late layers of the shared backbone rather than at the action interfaces. On standard benchmarks, Concertina achieves 98.15% average success on regular LIBERO, 85.9% on the 10,030-task LIBERO-Plus benchmark, and 4.142 average completed chain length on CALVIN ABC-D. Code: this https URL Hugging Face: this https URL

AI.tldr: Concertina is an embodied vision-language model that generates robot actions inside a shared diffusion VLM backbone, using continuous latent action tokens instead of a separate action expert. It reports 98.15% average success on regular LIBERO, 85.9% on LIBERO-Plus and 4.142 average completed chain length on CALVIN ABC-D.
AI.motivation: Existing VLA policies decouple manipulation from cognition: they either quantize actions into discrete tokens whose errors have no stable correspondence to physical displacements, or delegate trajectory generation to a separate action expert whose gradients compete with or are blocked from the VLM backbone.
AI.method: Each control timestep is encoded as one continuous latent action token in the backbone's hidden space, and the shared Transformer reconstructs temporally ordered action blocks with the same corrupt-and-reconstruct operator used for multimodal pretraining, with blockwise generation and physical-coordinate supervision and no separate action-generator layers.
AI.result: Active action projections account for 0.21% of the parameters of the 4.46B model, against 16.5%-35.1% dedicated action-expert capacity in representative continuous VLAs; the Action Interface Audit shows cross-time trajectory coupling emerges in middle and late backbone layers; success is 98.15% on regular LIBERO, 85.9% on the 10,030-task LIBERO-Plus and 4.142 average completed chain length on CALVIN ABC-D.
AI.conclusion: Embodying manipulation and cognition in one model, instead of bolting an action mechanism onto a VLM, is a viable route to an embodied VLM with minimal action-specific parameters.

title: Action-Conditioned VLM Monitoring for Autonomous Vehicle Semantic Anomalies
summary: We study action-conditioned monitoring of autonomous-vehicle behavior in semantically unusual driving scenes. The target is whether the executed ego action is appropriate for the scene: the same scene can admit both normal and anomalous behavior, so visual unusualness alone does not determine the monitoring label. A Vision-Language Model (VLM) first predicts the scene-required action from an outcome-hidden video window; the monitor then compares that expectation with the realized ego-motion trajectory under an explicit compatibility rule. To study this monitoring task, we contribute a six-field taxonomy of 112 paired scenarios spanning both failure polarities (42 derived from documented incidents), a generated video corpus with estimated trajectories, and an exploratory two-stage monitor on that corpus. On 235 clips from 15 scenario families, the two-stage protocol with a fixed T-2.5 s window obtains 83.0% accuracy and anomaly recall 0.773, versus 74.5% and 0.536 for a single-stage video-only baseline; specificity is 0.880 versus 0.928.

AI.tldr: The paper studies action-conditioned monitoring of autonomous-vehicle behaviour in semantically unusual driving scenes: a VLM first predicts the scene-required action and a monitor compares it with the realized ego trajectory. On 235 clips from 15 scenario families the two-stage protocol reaches 83.0% accuracy against 74.5% for a single-stage video-only baseline.
AI.motivation: Visual unusualness alone does not determine whether ego behaviour is anomalous, because the same scene can admit both normal and anomalous actions, so monitoring has to judge the executed action against what the scene requires.
AI.method: A VLM predicts the scene-required action from an outcome-hidden video window, and the monitor checks that expectation against the realized ego-motion trajectory under an explicit compatibility rule with a fixed T-2.5 s window; the authors also contribute a six-field taxonomy of 112 paired scenarios (42 derived from documented incidents), a generated video corpus with estimated trajectories, and an exploratory two-stage monitor.
AI.result: The two-stage protocol obtains 83.0% accuracy and anomaly recall 0.773, versus 74.5% and 0.536 for the single-stage video-only baseline; specificity is 0.880 versus 0.928.
AI.conclusion: Action-conditioned two-stage monitoring improves anomaly detection on this exploratory corpus, at some cost in specificity relative to the baseline.

title: OptIMerge: Optimization-Based Merging of Diffusion Models
summary: The arithmetic merging of weights from multiple task-specific models fine-tuned from a shared base model, commonly known as model souping, has emerged as a popular strategy for multi-task learning without the computational overhead of joint retraining. However, naive scalar weight averaging frequently leads to severe performance degradation when the constituent models learn structurally divergent feature representations, leading to destructive parameter interference. We study this problem in a largely unexplored setting: merging image-to-image (I2I) diffusion models fine-tuned for dense, pixel-accurate tasks such as image restoration. Unlike the large language models (LLMs) and text-to-image (T2I) diffusion models for which most merging methods were developed, I2I experts encode conflicting spatial priors (e.g., anisotropic motion-blur vs. isotropic defocus-blur) in their convolutional filters, where both naive soup and LLM-style element-wise merging introduce visible artifacts. We introduce OptIMerge, a gradient-based optimization framework: instead of relying on heuristic scalars, OptIMerge learns highly expressive, yet parameter-efficient merger coefficients by minimizing a multi-task diffusion loss over a small set of 100-500 images. OptIMerge parameterizes the merge with architecture-aware transformations: for attention layers, a structured low-rank feature alignment with explicit channel biases; for convolutional layers, per-kernel merger coefficients, and a low-rank Cayley transform that aligns channels by orthogonal rotation without distorting the filters. By keeping the experts frozen and optimizing only these lightweight merger parameters (equivalent to <0.4% of the network footprint), OptIMerge achieves simultaneous multi-task capabilities that rival computationally expensive joint training and decisively outperform zero-shot model soups.

AI.tldr: OptIMerge merges multiple image-to-image diffusion models fine-tuned for restoration tasks by learning lightweight merger coefficients through gradient-based optimisation, instead of heuristic scalar averaging. It aims to rival joint multi-task training and outperform zero-shot model soups.
AI.motivation: Naive weight averaging degrades severely when image-to-image diffusion experts encode conflicting spatial priors in their convolutional filters, a setting less studied than merging LLMs and text-to-image diffusion models.
AI.method: The experts stay frozen and only merger parameters are optimised by minimising a multi-task diffusion loss over 100-500 images; attention layers use a structured low-rank feature alignment with explicit channel biases, and convolutional layers use per-kernel merger coefficients with a low-rank Cayley transform that aligns channels by orthogonal rotation.
AI.result: The lightweight merger parameters are equivalent to under 0.4% of the network footprint, and the method is reported to achieve simultaneous multi-task capabilities that rival joint training and decisively outperform zero-shot model soups.
AI.conclusion: Gradient-based, architecture-aware merging with frozen experts is a parameter-efficient alternative to joint retraining for multi-task image-to-image diffusion models.

title: Training-Free Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning for Few-Step Autoregressive Video Diffusion
summary: Few-step autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models generate videos chunk by chunk and have made efficient video generation practical. However, further accelerating these models toward real-time generation remains challenging, as few-step distillation leaves little cross-step redundancy for existing training-free caching methods to exploit. We revisit this regime and identify two token-level redundancy patterns: cross-frame redundancy from static content shared across adjacent frames, and cross-step redundancy from tokens that converge early during denoising. Crucially, we find that early clean estimates along the model's own denoising trajectory provide an effective online signal for locating both patterns, requiring no retraining, auxiliary predictor, or reference video. Based on these findings, we propose PreSTP (Predictive Spatio-Temporal Token Pruning), a training-free framework that constructs a unified token-wise redundancy mask from cross-frame similarity and cross-step convergence. Tokens marked as redundant skip subsequent computation under a consistent last-computed-value restoration rule, and a content-adaptive mask reuse strategy further reduces dense probing cost. On 5-second generation, PreSTP achieves 1.52x-3.20x speedups and a better efficiency-fidelity trade-off than coarse-grained caching baselines such as TeaCache and FlowCache. On 30-second generation, it reaches up to 1.96x speedup while improving VBench-Long and suppressing long-horizon drift. Notably, it continues to reduce inference cost even in the extreme one-step regime, where cross-step redundancy vanishes entirely and coarse step-wise caching is no longer applicable.

AI.tldr: PreSTP is a training-free token pruning framework that accelerates few-step autoregressive video diffusion by skipping tokens that are redundant across frames or converge early during denoising. On 5-second generation it reports 1.52x-3.20x speedups.
AI.motivation: Few-step distillation leaves little cross-step redundancy for existing training-free caching methods to exploit, which makes further acceleration toward real-time generation difficult.
AI.method: Early clean estimates along the model's own denoising trajectory locate redundant tokens; a unified token-wise mask built from cross-frame similarity and cross-step convergence lets redundant tokens skip computation under a last-computed-value restoration rule, and a content-adaptive mask reuse strategy reduces the dense probing cost.
AI.result: On 5-second generation PreSTP achieves 1.52x-3.20x speedups with a better efficiency-fidelity trade-off than the coarse caching baselines TeaCache and FlowCache; on 30-second generation it reaches up to 1.96x speedup while improving VBench-Long and suppressing long-horizon drift; it still reduces cost in the one-step regime.
AI.conclusion: Token-level redundancy masks derived from the model's own denoising trajectory give a training-free route to faster few-step autoregressive video generation.

title: Improving Long-Tail Detection via Layout-Instruction Conditioned Diffusion Synthesis
summary: Synthetic data from diffusion models can improve object detection, but long-tail performance is still limited by scarce rare classes and inflexible conditioning (e.g., text-only or layout-only inputs). In this paper, we propose Tail-SD, a layout-instruction conditioned stable diffusion framework that supports text, layouts, or their hybrid, enabling controllable synthesis from boxes, masks, and/or prompts to better cover the long-tail objects. To train a single model across heterogeneous conditions, we introduce a multi-task cross-attention module and multi-task embedding tokens, improving generation quality and diversity. Extensive experiments on COCO and LVIS demonstrate that diffusion synthesis with hybrid conditioning consistently benefits detection, e.g., on LVIS val, it achieves +4.89% / +5.68% rare Box/Mask AP, highlighting strong potential for addressing long-tail challenges.

AI.tldr: Tail-SD is a layout-instruction conditioned Stable Diffusion framework that synthesizes training images from boxes, masks, prompts or their hybrid to improve long-tail object detection. Hybrid conditioning gives +4.89% / +5.68% rare Box/Mask AP on LVIS val.
AI.motivation: Synthetic data from diffusion models can improve detection, but long-tail performance is limited by scarce rare classes and by inflexible text-only or layout-only conditioning.
AI.method: A multi-task cross-attention module and multi-task embedding tokens let a single model train across heterogeneous conditions (text, layouts, or both), giving controllable synthesis from boxes, masks and/or prompts.
AI.result: On COCO and LVIS, diffusion synthesis with hybrid conditioning consistently benefits detection; on LVIS val it gives +4.89% / +5.68% rare Box/Mask AP.
AI.conclusion: Flexible layout-and-text conditioning makes synthetic data a stronger tool for covering long-tail object categories in detection.

title: MetricTrail: Revisiting the Power of Metric Depth and Local Optimization for Long-Sequence Streaming 3D Reconstruction
comment: Project Page: this https URL, Code: this https URL
summary: We present MetricTrail, a streaming system for accurate camera motion estimation and dense reconstruction from long monocular videos. To keep inference efficient over long sequences, we revisit DPVO's sparse local estimator. We find that single-image metric depth substantially improves its trajectory accuracy, without retraining the correspondence network or enlarging the optimization window. Metric predictions initialize patch depths and remain as soft constraints during optimization. We further improve correspondence estimation through learned adapters that augment matching features and recurrent context with frozen DINOv3 representations. The correspondence estimator and adapters are trained on diverse short clips without additional long-sequence training. This modular design also allows the depth provider to be independently upgraded and supports supplied camera intrinsics and calibrated stereo observations without retraining. Under the reported RGB-only protocols, MetricTrail achieves the lowest average trajectory error among evaluated methods on KITTI, Oxford Spires, and VBR. Pairing the estimated poses with single-image depth predictions also produces strong dense reconstruction on indoor and outdoor benchmarks and coherent reconstructions of in-the-wild videos. With supplied intrinsics, the system processes KITTI-02 at 12.70 FPS with 3.21 GB peak GPU memory.

AI.tldr: MetricTrail is a streaming system for camera motion estimation and dense reconstruction from long monocular videos that adds single-image metric depth to the DPVO sparse local estimator. Under RGB-only protocols it achieves the lowest average trajectory error among evaluated methods on KITTI, Oxford Spires and VBR.
AI.motivation: Long-sequence streaming reconstruction needs efficient inference, so the authors revisit DPVO's sparse local estimator and aim to improve its trajectory accuracy without enlarging the optimization window or retraining the correspondence network.
AI.method: Single-image metric depth initializes patch depths and stays as soft constraints during optimization; learned adapters augment matching features and recurrent context with frozen DINOv3 representations; the correspondence estimator and adapters are trained on diverse short clips, and the depth provider can be upgraded independently.
AI.result: MetricTrail achieves the lowest average trajectory error among evaluated methods on KITTI, Oxford Spires and VBR under RGB-only protocols, gives strong dense reconstruction on indoor and outdoor benchmarks, and with supplied intrinsics processes KITTI-02 at 12.70 FPS with 3.21 GB peak GPU memory.
AI.conclusion: Metric depth used as a soft constraint on a sparse local estimator improves long-video trajectories in a modular way that also supports supplied intrinsics and calibrated stereo without retraining.

title: Guidance Is a Field, Not a Scalar: Interval-Integrated Classifier-Free Guidance for One-Step Video Generation
summary: One-step generators built on MeanFlow synthesize a video in a single function evaluation, yet inherit a rigid treatment of classifier-free guidance (CFG): the guidance scale is frozen during training or, at best, exposed as a single scalar. This conflicts with mounting evidence that the optimal guidance is not a constant but a field that varies with the noise level, with spatial content, and, for video, with frame position. Every existing remedy presupposes a multi-step sampler along which guidance can be re-scheduled--an assumption one-step models violate by construction. We resolve this tension through a single observation: because the MeanFlow target is an integral over a noise interval, an arbitrary guidance field can be absorbed into the target itself and compiled into one evaluation. We formalize this as the interval-integrated CFG identity, prove that the compiled guidance carries no schedule-discretization error and can thus match or exceed any finite multi-step sampler, and instantiate it as AGAVE, which equips the average-velocity field with a learnable temporal schedule, a free motion-saliency spatial modulation, and a frame-position asymmetry. Adding fewer than ten scalars at zero inference cost, AGAVE surpasses all one-step baselines on VBench, UCF-101 and MSR-VTT while matching multi-step guided sampling. Project repository: this https URL.

AI.tldr: AGAVE applies interval-integrated classifier-free guidance to one-step MeanFlow video generators, compiling a learned guidance field into a single function evaluation at zero inference cost. It surpasses all one-step baselines on VBench, UCF-101 and MSR-VTT while matching multi-step guided sampling.
AI.motivation: One-step MeanFlow generators freeze classifier-free guidance or expose only a single scalar scale, whereas the optimal guidance varies with noise level, spatial content and frame position, and existing remedies assume a multi-step sampler.
AI.method: Because the MeanFlow target is an integral over a noise interval, an arbitrary guidance field can be absorbed into the target; the authors formalize this as the interval-integrated CFG identity and instantiate it as AGAVE, which adds a learnable temporal schedule, a motion-saliency spatial modulation and a frame-position asymmetry to the average-velocity field, with fewer than ten scalars.
AI.result: AGAVE surpasses all one-step baselines on VBench, UCF-101 and MSR-VTT while matching multi-step guided sampling, at zero inference cost; the authors state that the compiled guidance carries no schedule-discretization error and can match or exceed any finite multi-step sampler.
AI.conclusion: Guidance can be absorbed into the training target of one-step generators, giving guidance comparable to multi-step sampling in a single function evaluation.

title: Integrating Learned Priors through Prior-Space Reparameterization for Physically Based Inverse Rendering
summary: Physically based inverse rendering decomposes appearance into materials and illumination, an ambiguous problem for which learned material predictions provide useful prior information. Most existing methods incorporate these cues through auxiliary regularization losses, which alter the optimization objective and require balancing their influence against photometric fitting. We propose a prior-guided material reparameterization that uses the predicted feature relationships to restrict the optimization space while leaving the objective unchanged. We fuse multi-view material predictions onto a mesh and construct a permutohedral lattice in the resulting prior feature space. Surface points with similar predictions share material variables, which are optimized jointly with geometry and illumination using a purely photometric objective. Experiments with two learned predictors on three synthetic benchmarks and Stanford-ORB demonstrate improved material decomposition and relighting. Our method improves relighting PSNR by 1.5-2.5 dB over the strongest evaluated mesh-based baseline on Synthetic4Relight and TensoIR-Synthetic, and outperforms a regularization loss using the same prior in controlled comparisons. We further show that our reparameterization pools noisy photometric gradients, producing updates that are more consistent across sampled views. This consistency enables a shortened joint optimization schedule that takes less than a minute while retaining relighting quality above all evaluated baselines on TensoIR-Synthetic.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a prior-guided material reparameterization for physically based inverse rendering that makes surface points with similar learned material predictions share material variables, optimized under a purely photometric objective. It improves relighting PSNR by 1.5-2.5 dB over the strongest evaluated mesh-based baseline on Synthetic4Relight and TensoIR-Synthetic.
AI.motivation: Existing methods add learned material cues as auxiliary regularization losses, which alter the optimization objective and require balancing their influence against photometric fitting.
AI.method: Multi-view material predictions are fused onto a mesh and a permutohedral lattice is constructed in the resulting prior feature space; surface points with similar predictions share material variables, which are optimized jointly with geometry and illumination using only a photometric objective.
AI.result: Relighting PSNR improves by 1.5-2.5 dB over the strongest evaluated mesh-based baseline on Synthetic4Relight and TensoIR-Synthetic; the method outperforms a regularization loss using the same prior in controlled comparisons; a joint optimization schedule of under one minute retains relighting quality above all evaluated baselines on TensoIR-Synthetic.
AI.conclusion: Restricting the optimization space with the prior, rather than adding loss terms, improves material decomposition and relighting and yields more consistent multi-view updates.

title: Georeferenced Cross-View 3D Reconstruction from Ground and Satellite Images
summary: Georeferenced 3D reconstruction from ground images requires recovering not only the local scene geometry, but also localizing every camera center and 3D point in a geographic coordinate frame. Existing cross-view geo-localization methods are able to estimate the GPS coordinate of a single ground camera, but do not reconstruct dense 3D geometry, while recent feed-forward multi-view 3D reconstruction models predict point maps and camera poses only in a local coordinate frame. We introduce X-VGGT, a feed-forward cross-view geometry transformer that unifies these tasks by jointly processing a set of ground-level images and a georeferenced satellite image to predict ground-view camera poses, dense 3D point maps, and a scene-level transform parameterized by gravity, scale, yaw and translation. This transform projects the local reconstruction into the satellite plane, resulting in the geo-registration of all ground images with the georeferenced satellite image. We further propose an evaluation protocol for this joint task and show that, across multiple cross-view datasets, X-VGGT produces accurate georeferenced reconstructions and outperforms prior cross-view geo-localization and multi-view 3D reconstruction models.

AI.tldr: X-VGGT is a feed-forward cross-view geometry transformer that jointly processes ground images and a georeferenced satellite image to predict ground camera poses, dense point maps and a gravity-scale-yaw-translation transform that geo-registers the reconstruction. It outperforms prior cross-view geo-localization and multi-view reconstruction models across multiple datasets.
AI.motivation: Cross-view geo-localization estimates the GPS coordinate of a single ground camera but does not reconstruct dense 3D geometry, while feed-forward multi-view reconstruction predicts poses and point maps only in a local coordinate frame.
AI.method: The model jointly processes a set of ground-level images and a georeferenced satellite image, predicting ground-view camera poses, dense 3D point maps and a scene-level transform parameterized by gravity, scale, yaw and translation that projects the local reconstruction into the satellite plane.
AI.result: Across multiple cross-view datasets X-VGGT produces accurate georeferenced reconstructions and outperforms prior cross-view geo-localization and multi-view 3D reconstruction models; the authors also propose an evaluation protocol for this joint task.
AI.conclusion: A single feed-forward model can unify geo-localization and dense 3D reconstruction, registering ground images to a geographic frame.

title: Subspace Learning with Outlier Exposure for Out-of-Distribution Detection
summary: Out-of-Distribution (OoD) detection is pivotal for reliable deployments of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs), aiming to distinguish anomalous samples from the In-Distribution (InD) data in training. By introducing outliers as surrogate OoD data to finetune DNNs, Outlier Exposure (OE) has greatly advanced OoD detection in recent years. Existing OE-based research remains predominantly logit-centric, either by generating diverse outliers or by regularizing them with objectives operating at the prediction-output level. Nonetheless, these approaches leave much of the rich information in feature spaces untapped. In this work, we propose an OE-based detection framework, named RecOE, that learns appropriate feature subspaces from InD data and auxiliary outliers, such that the InD-OoD discrepancy can be effectively characterized through the learned feature subspaces. Specifically, the feature subspaces are optimized to capture the dominant variations of InD and outliers by minimizing reconstruction errors therein. Besides, a sample-level objective discourages reconstruction in the opposing subspace, while an orthogonality regularizer reduces subspace overlap, further promoting discriminative subspaces. At inference, the difference in reconstruction errors between the learned subspaces serves as the OoD detection score. Extensive experiments show the superiority of RecOE on multiple benchmarks, in which significant performance gains are achieved over recent strong baselines with only slight extra overhead from two small-size matrices of subspace bases. The source code is available at this https URL.
