AI.tldr: RecOE is an outlier-exposure out-of-distribution detection framework that learns feature subspaces from in-distribution data and auxiliary outliers and scores samples by the difference in their reconstruction errors across the two subspaces. It reports significant gains over recent strong baselines on multiple benchmarks with only slight extra overhead.
AI.motivation: Existing outlier-exposure methods are logit-centric, either generating diverse outliers or regularizing objectives at the prediction-output level, which leaves much of the rich feature-space information untapped.
AI.method: Feature subspaces are optimized to capture the dominant variations of in-distribution data and outliers by minimizing reconstruction errors; a sample-level objective discourages reconstruction in the opposing subspace, an orthogonality regularizer reduces subspace overlap, and the detection score is the difference in reconstruction errors between the learned subspaces.
AI.result: RecOE shows superior performance on multiple benchmarks, with significant gains over recent strong baselines and only slight extra overhead from two small-size matrices of subspace bases.
AI.conclusion: Learning discriminative feature subspaces offers a lightweight alternative to logit-level outlier exposure for OoD detection.

title: FisherDistill: Diffusion Distribution Distillation via Closed-Form Fisher Critics
summary: Recent advances in diffusion distillation have enabled high-quality image generation in only one or a few network function evaluations (NFEs). Despite their efficiency, aggressively distilled generators often retain a residual distribution gap from their multi-step teachers, motivating recent methods to introduce adversarial refinement with a learned discriminator. In this work, we ask whether such refinement necessarily requires a learned adversarial discriminator. We introduce \textbf{FisherDistill}, a simple alternative based on Fisher linear discriminant analysis. Using intermediate representations from the frozen teacher, we estimate the first- and second-order statistics of real and generated samples and derive a closed-form Fisher direction that maximally separates their feature distributions relative to within-class variation. This direction provides a lightweight refinement signal that complements the original distillation objective without requiring an additional adversarial discriminator or its optimization loop. Across multiple distillation frameworks, our approach consistently improves generation quality over their respective distilled baselines and substantially closes the gap to adversarially refined counterparts. Code: this https URL

AI.tldr: FisherDistill refines a distilled diffusion generator with a closed-form Fisher discriminant direction computed from the frozen teacher's features, avoiding a learned adversarial discriminator. It consistently improves generation quality over its distilled baselines across multiple distillation frameworks and substantially closes the gap to adversarially refined counterparts.
AI.motivation: Aggressively distilled one- or few-step generators retain a residual distribution gap from their multi-step teachers, and recent methods close it with adversarial refinement using a learned discriminator.
AI.method: Using intermediate representations from the frozen teacher, first- and second-order statistics of real and generated samples are estimated, and a closed-form Fisher direction is derived that maximally separates their feature distributions relative to within-class variation; this direction is a refinement signal added to the original distillation objective.
AI.result: Across multiple distillation frameworks the approach consistently improves generation quality over the respective distilled baselines and substantially closes the gap to adversarially refined counterparts.
AI.conclusion: Adversarial refinement is not strictly necessary for closing the distribution gap in diffusion distillation, since a closed-form Fisher signal can serve as a lightweight alternative.

title: Towards Real-Time Full-Waveform LiDAR Transformers via Intensity-Guided Token Reduction and Physics-Aware Augmentation
summary: LiDAR is a critical sensor for autonomous driving and robotics, yet it remains vulnerable to adverse conditions such as fog, rain, transparent objects, and low-reflectance surfaces. Full-waveform LiDAR (FWL) addresses these limitations by capturing the complete return waveform as a histogram, preserving rich reflection characteristics including multi-path echoes and weak signals. While recent Transformer-based approaches have demonstrated promise on FWL data, two fundamental bottlenecks remain: high computational cost from redundant tokens in low-intensity background regions, and limited generalization due to scarce annotated training data. We address both bottlenecks by exploiting the physical structure inherent to FWL data. First, we propose FWL-ToPM, a token pruning and merging mechanism that leverages intensity distributions to selectively reduce tokens while retaining critical waveform content. Second, we introduce FWLAug, a data augmentation framework designed as a regularization method that preserves waveform structure, retaining the Time-of-Flight waveform of each ray and the frustum geometry, to improve generalization to unseen scenes. Evaluated on the Ghost-FWL benchmark, FWL-ToPM achieves over 8 times speedup at real-time throughput alongside a nearly 9-point F1 gain over the prior state of the art, establishing the first real-time FWL Transformer that simultaneously improves accuracy. FWLAug further improves performance on both the standard benchmark and an out-of-distribution test set of unseen scenes. Together, these methods push FWL-based perception toward practical deployment. The code and the OOD dataset are publicly available and can be accessed via the project page: this https URL

AI.tldr: The paper proposes FWL-ToPM, an intensity-guided token pruning and merging mechanism, and FWLAug, a waveform-preserving augmentation, for full-waveform LiDAR Transformers. On Ghost-FWL, FWL-ToPM achieves over 8 times speedup at real-time throughput with a nearly 9-point F1 gain over the prior state of the art.
AI.motivation: FWL Transformers face high computational cost from redundant tokens in low-intensity background regions and limited generalization due to scarce annotated training data.
AI.method: FWL-ToPM uses intensity distributions to selectively reduce tokens while retaining critical waveform content; FWLAug is a regularization-style augmentation that preserves each ray's Time-of-Flight waveform and the frustum geometry.
AI.result: On Ghost-FWL, FWL-ToPM achieves over 8 times speedup at real-time throughput with a nearly 9-point F1 gain over the prior state of the art, the first real-time FWL Transformer that also improves accuracy; FWLAug further improves performance on the standard benchmark and on an out-of-distribution test set of unseen scenes.
AI.conclusion: Exploiting the physical structure of FWL data pushes waveform-based perception toward practical deployment, with code and the OOD dataset publicly available.

title: TRACEMARK: Editor-Aware Watermarking for User Attribution in Text-Guided Image Editing
summary: An image editing service records which user requests each edit, but the edited image itself does not contain this account information. Once the image is downloaded and shared, the service cannot identify the requesting user from the image alone. Embedding a user-specific watermark could enable such attribution, but semantic editing may erase the signal. We propose Tracemark, an editor-aware watermarking framework for identifying users from edited images. A shared encoder embeds a user-specific signal before editing, and a shared detector recovers the user by comparing features of the edited image with learned reference vectors. Both components are trained jointly through an editor with fixed parameters. User identification errors encourage the encoder to produce watermarks that survive editing, while fidelity losses limit changes to the input image and intended edit. Each image domain and editing instruction uses a separately trained model shared across registered users. Experiments on three image domains show that editor-aware training improves user recovery with both reference-vector matching and binary watermark decoding. Separately trained models reach 87.5% mean identification accuracy among 500 users. When tested with a different editor without retraining, the watermark modules still recover user information. These results demonstrate that learning watermarks through the editing process enables user attribution without modifying the editor.

AI.tldr: TRACEMARK is an editor-aware watermarking framework that embeds a user-specific signal before text-guided image editing, so that an edited image can be traced back to the requesting user. Separately trained models reach 87.5% mean identification accuracy among 500 users.
AI.motivation: An image editing service records which user requested each edit, but the edited image carries no account information, and semantic editing may erase a conventional watermark signal.
AI.method: A shared encoder embeds a user-specific signal before editing and a shared detector recovers the user by comparing features of the edited image with learned reference vectors; both are trained jointly through a fixed-parameter editor, with identification errors encouraging watermarks that survive editing and fidelity losses limiting changes to the input and intended edit.
AI.result: Editor-aware training improves user recovery in three image domains with both reference-vector matching and binary watermark decoding; separately trained models reach 87.5% mean identification accuracy among 500 users; with a different editor and no retraining the watermark modules still recover user information.
AI.conclusion: Learning watermarks through the editing process enables user attribution without modifying the editor.

title: Neural Image Compression with Internal-External Prior Fusion and Alignment
comment: IEEE International Conference on Visual Communications and Image Processing 2026 (VCIP 2026)
summary: Existing context models for learned image com- pression rely primarily on internal priors from the current image, overlooking common patterns and typical textures shared across natural images. To address this limitation, we propose an Internal-External Prior Fusion-Alignment (IE-PFA) context model built upon quadtree spatial-channel joint modeling, where a learnable dictionary shared by the encoder and decoder serves as an external prior. Specifically, an RWKV-based Spatial- Channel Prior Fusion (RSCPF) module efficiently fuses inter- nal and external priors along spatial and channel dimensions with linear complexity, while a training-only Self-Distilled Prior Alignment (SDPA) mechanism aligns them without inference overhead. Moreover, our model supports variable-rate coding over 64 quality levels within a single network and is accelerated by custom CUDA operators. Experiments on seven benchmarks demonstrate state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance, achiev- ing an average BD-Rate saving of 21.65% over VTM-22.0-Intra, with only 29.9M parameters and the fastest coding speed among advanced neural codecs (61 ms encoding and 52 ms decoding). Code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: IE-PFA is a learned image compression context model that fuses internal priors from the current image with a shared learnable external dictionary prior, aligned by a training-only mechanism. It reports an average 21.65% BD-Rate saving over VTM-22.0-Intra with 29.9M parameters.
AI.motivation: Context models for learned image compression rely mainly on internal priors from the current image and overlook common patterns and typical textures shared across natural images.
AI.method: The IE-PFA context model is built on quadtree spatial-channel joint modeling with a learnable dictionary shared by encoder and decoder as an external prior; an RWKV-based Spatial-Channel Prior Fusion module fuses internal and external priors with linear complexity, a training-only Self-Distilled Prior Alignment aligns them without inference overhead, and one network supports 64 quality levels with custom CUDA operators.
AI.result: Across seven benchmarks the model achieves an average BD-Rate saving of 21.65% over VTM-22.0-Intra with 29.9M parameters and the fastest coding speed among advanced neural codecs (61 ms encoding and 52 ms decoding).
AI.conclusion: Combining internal and shared external priors yields state-of-the-art rate-distortion performance at practical coding speed.

title: UniGADD: Universal Generator-Agnostic Deepfake Detector
summary: In this paper, we introduce Universal Generator-Agnostic Deepfake Detector (UniGADD), a novel method that employs supervised learning to achieve high accuracy on known deepfake generators, while maintaining robust performance on previously unseen ones. The proposed approach follows a two-stage optimisation process. In the first stage, a contrastive loss encourages the model to learn discriminative feature embeddings from real and known fake images, resulting in strong performance within the training domain. In the second stage, the embedding space is refined by promoting inter-cluster separation and intra-cluster compactness, applied exclusively to real samples. This refinement enhances generalisability, enabling the method to exhibit improved robustness against unseen deepfake generation techniques. UniGADD achieves accuracy on par with state-of-the-art methods for known generators, while significantly outperforming them on unseen cases, demonstrating its scalability and practical applicability for adversarial content detection.

AI.tldr: UniGADD is a two-stage supervised deepfake detector that first uses contrastive learning on real and known fake images and then refines the embedding space on real samples only. It matches state-of-the-art accuracy on known generators and significantly outperforms them on unseen generators.
AI.motivation: Deepfake detectors that perform strongly on known generators often fail to generalize to previously unseen generation techniques.
AI.method: Stage one applies a contrastive loss to learn discriminative feature embeddings from real and known fake images; stage two promotes inter-cluster separation and intra-cluster compactness, applied exclusively to real samples.
AI.result: UniGADD achieves accuracy on par with state-of-the-art methods for known generators while significantly outperforming them on unseen generation techniques.
AI.conclusion: Refining the embedding space of real samples enhances generalizability, supporting scalable and practical detection of adversarial content.

title: Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling with Target-Aware Bounded Optimization for Visual Generation
summary: Post-training aims to enhance desired attributes in visual generative models while preserving their general generation capabilities. Reward-guided post-training faces two challenges: real training data may mismatch the generator's output distribution, and attribute supervision may be confounded by unrelated content. Unbounded reward maximization can also cause overoptimization and degrade generation quality. We propose a framework combining Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling (GARM) and Target-Aware Bounded Optimization (TABO). GARM mitigates distribution mismatch through generator-support matching and reduces content confounding using content-matched real contrasts, yielding generator-relevant, attribute-focused reward supervision. TABO maps the learned reward to a smooth, upper-bounded function calibrated from real target-positive examples. This transformation is independent of the optimization algorithm and supports both direct reward-gradient and policy-based optimization. We further introduce Target-Aware GRPO (TA-GRPO), an adaptation of Flow-GRPO that combines fixed stage-wise advantage scaling, a generator-to-target curriculum, and timestep-balanced credit assignment for flow-based video optimization. Experiments show that GARM improves target-attribute expression while maintaining competitive generation quality. TABO better balances attribute enhancement and visual quality than unconstrained reward maximization, while TA-GRPO improves target enhancement over vanilla Flow-GRPO and reduces unintended attribute leakage on neutral prompts. These results highlight the importance of generator-aligned reward supervision and controlled, data-calibrated optimization for targeted visual generation.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes Generator-Aligned Reward Modeling (GARM) and Target-Aware Bounded Optimization (TABO) for reward-guided post-training of visual generators, along with TA-GRPO for flow-based video optimization. Experiments show better target-attribute expression while keeping generation quality, and less attribute leakage on neutral prompts than vanilla Flow-GRPO.
AI.motivation: Real training data may mismatch the generator's output distribution, attribute supervision may be confounded by unrelated content, and unbounded reward maximization can cause overoptimization that degrades generation quality.
AI.method: GARM uses generator-support matching and content-matched real contrasts to obtain generator-relevant, attribute-focused reward supervision; TABO maps the learned reward to a smooth, upper-bounded function calibrated on real target-positive examples and is independent of the optimization algorithm; TA-GRPO adapts Flow-GRPO with fixed stage-wise advantage scaling, a generator-to-target curriculum and timestep-balanced credit assignment.
AI.result: GARM improves target-attribute expression while maintaining competitive generation quality; TABO balances attribute enhancement and visual quality better than unconstrained reward maximization; TA-GRPO improves target enhancement over vanilla Flow-GRPO and reduces unintended attribute leakage on neutral prompts.
AI.conclusion: Generator-aligned reward supervision and controlled, data-calibrated optimization matter for targeted visual generation.

title: ArtCrafter: Feed-Forward Generation of Articulated 3D Object with Analytic Joint Derivation
summary: Articulated 3D assets are essential for robotic simulation and training, yet their generation from casual images poses a key challenge: recovering part geometry and kinematics that remain mutually consistent. We present ArtCrafter, a novel feed-forward generative model for controllable generation of articulated 3D objects from a pair of images, one depicting the object in the rest state and the other in the open state. At the core of ArtCrafter is a DiT-based generative model that jointly produces part-level meshes for both articulation states in a single forward pass. Inspired by Slot Attention, its denoising process operates on a $1+2N$ slot layout comprising one shared base slot and $N$ paired rest/open slots, encouraging each pair to bind to the same kinematic part. To ensure geometrically consistent and disjoint part generation, we introduce Triplet Attention to enforce cross-state geometric consistency between paired rest/open slots anchored through the shared base slot, and a repulsion loss $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{rep}}$ on decoded part point clouds to prevent inter-part penetration throughout denoising. Given the resulting paired meshes, URDF joint parameters---type, axis, origin, and range---are derived analytically from the rigid transformation between each rest/open pair, providing an interpretable alternative to learned joint-parameter regression. Extensive experiments on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets demonstrate that ArtCrafter outperforms existing method under the same dual-state setting in geometry quality and articulation precision, while remaining competitive with methods operating under different input settings and paradigms.

AI.tldr: ArtCrafter is a feed-forward DiT-based model that generates articulated 3D objects from a pair of rest-state and open-state images, producing paired part meshes in a single pass and deriving URDF joint parameters analytically from the rigid transformations. It outperforms existing methods under the same dual-state setting in geometry quality and articulation precision.
AI.motivation: Articulated 3D assets for robotic simulation need part geometry and kinematics that remain mutually consistent, which is hard to recover from casual images.
AI.method: A DiT-based generator denoises a 1+2N slot layout, one shared base slot and N paired rest/open slots inspired by Slot Attention; Triplet Attention enforces cross-state geometric consistency anchored through the base slot, and a repulsion loss on decoded part point clouds prevents inter-part penetration; URDF joint type, axis, origin and range are derived from the rigid transformation between each rest/open pair.
AI.result: ArtCrafter outperforms existing methods under the same dual-state setting in geometry quality and articulation precision on in-distribution and out-of-distribution datasets, and remains competitive with methods that use different input settings and paradigms.
AI.conclusion: Analytic joint derivation from paired meshes is an interpretable alternative to learned joint-parameter regression for generating articulated objects.

title: Which Objects Stay? Learning Hierarchical Persistence Beliefs for Lifelong Open-Vocabulary Object Maps
summary: Lifelong object maps must estimate whether an object remains at its previously observed location after it leaves view. Existing persistence filters rely on class-based survival priors, making them difficult to apply reliably in open-vocabulary settings. We introduce HiPer, a hierarchical persistence filter that derives persistence beliefs directly from data rather than semantic categories. For a new object, HiPer retrieves visually and geometrically similar training instances and estimates an initial survival rate from their observed histories, without requiring class labels. This estimate initializes a conjugate Beta belief over the object's survival probability, which is updated in closed form using detections and missed observations under Rosen's persistence-filter framework. When an object is re-identified at a new location, its persistence belief is transferred with the object, enabling the map to learn object-specific mobility over time. Experiments on 120 held-out simulated sequences show that HiPer consistently achieves the best performance among competing methods. Retrieval-based priors outperform CLIP-derived label priors, and object-specific online learning provides further gains. Results on 47 held-out 3RScan environments demonstrate that the proposed retrieval-based prior also outperforms state-of-the-art baselines in real-world settings.

AI.tldr: HiPer is a lifelong object-map persistence filter that sets each object's survival belief from retrieved visually and geometrically similar training instances instead of class labels, and it outperforms competing methods on simulated and real 3RScan data.
AI.motivation: Persistence filters for lifelong object maps rely on class-based survival priors, which are hard to apply reliably in open-vocabulary settings.
AI.method: For a new object, HiPer retrieves similar training instances and estimates an initial survival rate from their observed histories; this initializes a conjugate Beta belief that is updated in closed form from detections and missed observations under Rosen's persistence-filter framework. When an object is re-identified at a new location, its belief is transferred with it, so the map learns object-specific mobility over time.
AI.result: On 120 held-out simulated sequences HiPer achieves the best performance among competing methods; retrieval-based priors outperform CLIP-derived label priors, and object-specific online learning gives further gains. On 47 held-out 3RScan environments the retrieval-based prior also outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
AI.conclusion: Deriving persistence beliefs directly from data rather than semantic categories makes object-map persistence filtering workable in open-vocabulary settings.

title: CoGenRec: A Unified Generative Framework for Complementary Vision Reconstruction
summary: Capturing scenes with extreme motion and high dynamic range is fundamentally constrained by trade-offs among temporal resolution, spatial detail, signal-to-noise ratio, and dynamic range under practical bandwidth, power, and quantum-efficiency limits. Conventional frame-based cameras therefore suffer from temporal undersampling, exposure-induced motion blur, and sensor saturation. The Complementary Vision Sensor (CVS) addresses these limitations by decomposing visual information across two complementary pathways, a spatially dense, temporally sparse, long-exposure RGB pathway and a temporally dense, spatially sparse, short-exposure patiotemporal difference pathway. Their complementary measurements provide appearance, structural, and motion cues across a wide dynamic range that enable reconstruction beyond conventional imaging. We present CoGenRec, a complementarity-driven generative reconstruction framework that unifies video deblurring, high-temporal-resolution frame interpolation, and HDR fusion. CoGenRec encodes complementary measurements into multi-scale spatiotemporal features using exposure-aware appearance modeling and bidirectional temporal propagation. These features constrain a video diffusion model and are injected into the VAE decoder to recover fine structures lost during latent-space compression, combining the scene fidelity of physical measurements with the appearance recovery capabilities of learned video priors. On SportsSloMo-CVS, CoGenRec improves PSNR over the strongest general-purpose baseline by 4.40 dB for deblurring, 3.89 dB for frame interpolation, and 5.04 dB for HDR fusion, respectively. It also achieves strong perceptual quality on 129 unseen scenes captured with real CVS. These results establish a unified approach to advance high-quality reconstruction under challenging motion and illumination conditions. Project page: this https URL.

AI.tldr: CoGenRec is a generative framework that jointly performs video deblurring, high-temporal-resolution frame interpolation and HDR fusion from Complementary Vision Sensor measurements. It improves PSNR over the strongest general-purpose baseline by 4.40 dB, 3.89 dB and 5.04 dB on these three tasks.
AI.motivation: Frame-based cameras suffer temporal undersampling, motion blur and sensor saturation under extreme motion and high dynamic range, and existing reconstruction methods do not exploit the complementary dense long-exposure and sparse short-exposure pathways of the CVS.
AI.method: CoGenRec encodes the two complementary measurement streams into multi-scale spatiotemporal features using exposure-aware appearance modeling and bidirectional temporal propagation. These features constrain a video diffusion model and are injected into the VAE decoder to recover fine structures lost during latent-space compression.
AI.result: On SportsSloMo-CVS, PSNR gains over the strongest general-purpose baseline are 4.40 dB for deblurring, 3.89 dB for frame interpolation and 5.04 dB for HDR fusion; the method also achieves strong perceptual quality on 129 unseen scenes captured with a real CVS.
AI.conclusion: A unified generative approach can reconstruct high-quality video under challenging motion and illumination by combining the scene fidelity of physical measurements with the appearance priors of learned video models.

title: Egocentric Action Recognition with Objects and Vision-Language Affordances
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures. Under review at IEEE FG 2027
summary: Action recognition, and more specifically egocentric action recognition, is a core task in computer vision, with applications such as monitoring the daily life activities of elderly people and task assistance. Recent methods rely on visual modalities such as RGB video or depth. However, in egocentric video, an action is largely defined by its objects, which these methods rarely model. We propose a method that combines a frozen SlowFast video expert with an attention-based object expert by late fusion. Each object is represented with its affordances, that is, what can be done with it, generated zero-shot by a vision-language model. Since datasets such as MECCANO annotate only the objects involved in each action, evaluating with these boxes tells the model which objects are active. We therefore train on annotated boxes and evaluate the method with detections from the official active-object detector, and with annotated boxes as an upper bound. Without affordances, our fusion reaches 68.4% Top-1 with annotated boxes but 49.0% with detections. About half of this drop comes from non-active detections. To remove them, the same vision-language model generates an interaction affordance that decides whether a hand is manipulating each detected object. On MECCANO, objects raise the Top-1 of the video expert from 44.9% to 49.0%, and the two affordances raise it to 49.9%, above SlowFast and object-aware RGB baselines. Code will be released upon acceptance.

AI.tldr: The paper adds object affordances generated zero-shot by a vision-language model to a late fusion of a frozen SlowFast video expert and an attention-based object expert, improving egocentric action recognition on MECCANO. A second, interaction affordance further filters out inactive detected objects.
AI.motivation: Egocentric action recognition methods rely on RGB or depth and rarely model the objects that define an action; when detected rather than annotated objects are used, accuracy drops sharply, and about half of that drop comes from non-active detections.
AI.method: A frozen SlowFast video expert is late-fused with an attention-based object expert in which each object is represented by an affordance (what can be done with it) generated zero-shot by a vision-language model. The same model generates an interaction affordance that decides whether a hand is manipulating each detected object. Training uses annotated boxes; evaluation uses detections from the official active-object detector, with annotated boxes as an upper bound.
AI.result: With annotated boxes the fusion reaches 68.4% Top-1 without affordances but 49.0% with detections. On MECCANO, objects raise the video expert's Top-1 from 44.9% to 49.0%, and the two affordances raise it to 49.9%, above SlowFast and object-aware RGB baselines.
AI.conclusion: Vision-language affordances give a zero-shot way to model active objects for egocentric action recognition, although the gap between annotated and detected objects remains large.

title: GEKey: Learning Geodesic Eccentric 3D Keypoints via Self-Supervision
summary: Point clouds represent 3D object geometry as sets of spatial coordinates. A fundamental task in their analysis is keypoint detection, i.e., identifying a sparse subset of points that captures the most salient features. While supervised methods rely on manual annotations, unsupervised approaches leverage intrinsic geometric properties to localize keypoints without human input. We introduce GEKey, a self-supervised framework that uses the geodesic eccentricity transform, an SE(3)-invariant geometric measure, to identify instance-specific salient points. These points serve as pseudo-labels to train a model that aligns its predictions with the object's intrinsic structure. GEKey is simple, efficient, and robust, preserving intra-class variation by balancing instance-specific and category-level structure. Extensive experiments on ShapeNetCoreV2, KeypointNet, CAPE, ITOP, and DeformingThings4D show state-of-the-art performance in both keypoint detection and alignment, with strong resilience to noise, downsampling, deformations, and real-world conditions. The code and pretrained models are available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: GEKey is a self-supervised method that detects 3D keypoints on point clouds by using the geodesic eccentricity transform, an SE(3)-invariant measure, to generate pseudo-labels for training. It reports state-of-the-art keypoint detection and alignment on five datasets.
AI.motivation: Supervised keypoint detectors need manual annotation, while existing unsupervised approaches must localize salient points without human input and still preserve intra-class variation.
AI.method: The geodesic eccentricity transform identifies instance-specific salient points that serve as pseudo-labels for training a model to align its predictions with the object's intrinsic structure. The approach balances instance-specific and category-level structure.
AI.result: Experiments on ShapeNetCoreV2, KeypointNet, CAPE, ITOP and DeformingThings4D show state-of-the-art keypoint detection and alignment, with strong resilience to noise, downsampling, deformations and real-world conditions.
AI.conclusion: Intrinsic geodesic eccentricity offers a simple, efficient and robust self-supervised signal for keypoints that requires no annotation.

title: DEQ-Det: Dual Evidence Queries for Few-Shot Analog IC Device Detection
summary: Detecting analog integrated circuit (IC) devices in layout images supports circuit analysis and inspection. With only a few annotated examples, variation in device geometry and visual similarity to dummy or routing structures make reliable detection difficult. Foreground similarity alone can highlight plausible targets without distinguishing them from competing layout patterns. We propose Dual Evidence Queries for Detection (DEQ-Det), which constructs complementary foreground and background references from the same support images without additional annotations. Foreground references capture target morphology, while selected background references characterize surrounding layout patterns. Both sources guide query selection and region verification, combining target appearance with layout context. Across five held-out device categories and three random seeds, DEQ-Det achieves macro AP50 of 39.41 and 53.03 at 10 and 30 shots, exceeding the strongest listed baselines by 3.97 and 9.71 points, respectively. A matched 30-shot ablation further shows that RoI background evidence reduces pooled false positives at comparable recall, supporting its role in interference suppression.

AI.tldr: DEQ-Det is a few-shot detector for analog IC devices in layout images that builds foreground and background reference evidence from the same support images. It exceeds the strongest listed baselines by 3.97 and 9.71 macro AP50 points at 10 and 30 shots.
AI.motivation: With few annotated examples, device geometry varies and dummy or routing structures look visually similar to targets; foreground similarity alone highlights plausible targets but cannot separate them from competing layout patterns.
AI.method: Dual Evidence Queries for Detection (DEQ-Det) constructs complementary foreground references, which capture target morphology, and background references selected from surrounding layout, which characterize interfering patterns, with no additional annotations. Both sources guide query selection and region verification.
AI.result: Across five held-out device categories and three random seeds, macro AP50 is 39.41 at 10 shots and 53.03 at 30 shots. A matched 30-shot ablation shows that RoI background evidence reduces pooled false positives at comparable recall.
AI.conclusion: Background evidence drawn from the same support images helps suppress layout interference, supporting combined target and context reasoning for few-shot IC device detection.

title: ReferClaw: Disambiguating User Intent for Egocentric Assistance
summary: Users of egocentric AI assistants often ask short, ambiguous questions whose intended referents cannot be uniquely resolved from video and dialogue history. For example, "Where did I leave it?" may refer to several previously handled objects. Existing VideoQA systems typically commit to a single interpretation, risking plausible but intention-misaligned answers. We introduce ReferClaw, an agentic framework that formulates egocentric streaming QA as an interactive process: the assistant asks clarifying questions to resolve user intent before answering. Three cooperating agents identify candidate interpretations, request clarification, and generate answers grounded in the resolved intent and visual evidence. A bounded, cost-aware policy balances expected information gain against user effort while limiting clarification turns and question complexity. Referclaw learns from interaction through intent-specific skill updates and process-reward-guided policy optimization with agent-level credit assignment. Evaluations on augmented egocentric QA benchmarks demonstrate improved answer accuracy and joint answer-and-grounding performance over existing baselines, alongside zero-shot transfer across datasets. These findings support interactive clarification as a practical approach to resolving online user intent in egocentric streaming assistance.

AI.tldr: ReferClaw is an agentic framework that turns egocentric streaming QA into an interactive process, in which the assistant asks clarifying questions to resolve ambiguous references before answering. It improves answer accuracy and joint answer-and-grounding performance and transfers zero-shot across datasets.
AI.motivation: Short, ambiguous questions such as "Where did I leave it?" can refer to several previously handled objects, and VideoQA systems that commit to a single interpretation risk plausible but intention-misaligned answers.
AI.method: Three cooperating agents identify candidate interpretations, request clarification and generate answers grounded in the resolved intent and visual evidence. A bounded, cost-aware policy balances expected information gain against user effort while limiting clarification turns and question complexity. The system learns from interaction through intent-specific skill updates and process-reward-guided policy optimization with agent-level credit assignment.
AI.result: Evaluations on augmented egocentric QA benchmarks show improved answer accuracy and joint answer-and-grounding performance over existing baselines, along with zero-shot transfer across datasets.
AI.conclusion: Interactive clarification is presented as a practical way to resolve online user intent in egocentric streaming assistance.

title: FlyingDrones: A Dataset and Benchmark for Optical Flow Estimation from UAV motion
summary: Optical flow is an important cue for drone analysis in aerial surveillance, airspace monitoring, and long-range target tracking, where motion remains informative when appearance is weak. Estimating the motion of small Unmanned Aerial Vehicles, however, is difficult because distant targets occupy few pixels, have low contrast, and move against complex dynamic backgrounds. Standard optical-flow benchmarks emphasize large, object-centric motions and therefore do not characterize distant aerial targets well. We introduce FlyingDrones, a generated benchmark with dense ground-truth optical flow and segmentation masks derived from physically based rendering, and define resolution-normalized metrics (EPE Norm) that normalize flow by image dimensions. We evaluate 16 state-of-the-art model families on a motion- and size-stratified subset of 999 flow pairs at three resolutions. Every family recovers drone motion better than the zero-flow reference, but the gap between families widens with resolution: at 1920x1080, global-matching, recurrent, transformer, and short-window temporal models separate clearly from pyramid, classical, self-supervised, lightweight, and diffusion models. Within-family checkpoint spread is comparable to or larger than between-family spread, so the training curriculum is as important as the architecture. Two complementary studies test the benchmark beyond synthetic accuracy: a ground-truth-free motion-alignment evaluation on 21 cameras of real UAV footage shows that the synthetic ranking carries a moderate, significant signal about real-world performance (Spearman \r{ho} = 0.63 over 41 checkpoints) while the exact top ranks differ, and a fine-tuning study shows that 800 FlyingDrones pairs reduce held-out drone-region error by up to 37% and improve drone localization on the real footage for all four architectures tested.

AI.tldr: FlyingDrones is a rendered optical-flow benchmark for small UAVs with dense ground truth and resolution-normalized EPE metrics, used to evaluate 16 model families. Synthetic rankings correlate moderately with real UAV footage, and fine-tuning on 800 pairs reduces held-out drone-region error by up to 37%.
AI.motivation: Standard optical-flow benchmarks emphasize large, object-centric motion and do not characterize distant aerial targets, which occupy few pixels, have low contrast and move against dynamic backgrounds.
AI.method: The benchmark is generated with physically based rendering and provides dense flow and segmentation masks; EPE Norm normalizes flow by image dimensions. Sixteen model families are evaluated on a motion- and size-stratified subset of 999 flow pairs at three resolutions. Two complementary studies follow: a ground-truth-free motion-alignment evaluation on 21 real UAV cameras, and a fine-tuning study.
AI.result: Every family beats the zero-flow reference, and the gap between families widens with resolution; within-family checkpoint spread is comparable to or larger than between-family spread. The synthetic ranking carries a moderate, significant signal about real footage (Spearman rho = 0.63 over 41 checkpoints), and 800 FlyingDrones pairs reduce held-out drone-region error by up to 37% and improve real-footage drone localization for all four architectures tested.
AI.conclusion: The training curriculum matters as much as architecture, and the synthetic benchmark gives a useful, though imperfect, signal for real UAV flow performance.

title: AffineGS: Unlocking Accurate Geometry in 3DGS via Spatially Varying Affine Rectification
comment: Accpeted to NeurIPS 2026. Project page: this https URL
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has become the leading approach for photorealistic novel view synthesis, yet its geometric accuracy lags behind its visual quality. Existing depth-guided methods attempt to resolve this by regularizing the optimization with monocular depth priors, typically using a single global scale-and-shift alignment. Crucially, we discover a fundamental flaw in this assumption: modern monocular depth networks systematically exhibit region-dependent, piecewise-linear distortions. This discovery invalidates standard global alignment strategies, which warp scene geometry by enforcing a single transform. To address this, we introduce a spatially varying affine rectification model that corrects monocular disparity into consistent metric depth using regionally smooth, edge-aware fields. We further derive a normal-aware regularizer that uses spatial gradients to couple the rectified disparity with 3DGS depth and normals. Across diverse experimental settings, our sensor-free method shows strong photometric quality of Gaussian Splatting while substantially improving geometric accuracy and outperforming state-of-the art geometry-focused methods.

AI.tldr: AffineGS corrects monocular depth with a spatially varying affine rectification and a normal-aware regularizer, improving the geometric accuracy of 3D Gaussian Splatting while keeping photometric quality. It outperforms state-of-the-art geometry-focused methods.
AI.motivation: Depth-guided 3DGS methods regularize optimization with a single global scale-and-shift alignment, but modern monocular depth networks show region-dependent, piecewise-linear distortions that a global transform cannot correct.
AI.method: A spatially varying affine rectification model maps monocular disparity to consistent metric depth using regionally smooth, edge-aware fields. A normal-aware regularizer uses spatial gradients to couple the rectified disparity with 3DGS depth and normals. The method is sensor-free.
AI.result: Across diverse experimental settings the method shows strong photometric quality while substantially improving geometric accuracy, outperforming state-of-the-art geometry-focused methods; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Replacing global depth alignment with spatially varying rectification yields more accurate geometry for Gaussian Splatting without sacrificing visual quality.

title: Fast and Accurate Hand Estimation in Pixels, Interaction and World Space
comment: 10 pages of main text plus 15 pages of supplementary material; 5 figures; 12 tables; code available at this https URL
summary: Monocular hand mesh estimators commonly predict rig parameters and project the mesh to obtain 2D keypoints. We find that directly predicted 3D joints agree better with 2D predictions, and fitting a mesh to predicted points reduces mesh error. We present FAH (Fast and Accurate Hand Estimation), a family of models built on SAM 3D Body's hand branch through fine-tuning and feature distillation. The models predict corresponding 2D and 3D joints and surface points, fit MANO or MHR-Hand, and optionally estimate anatomical parts and contact without object geometry at inference. Causal refinement reduces acceleration error, and camera estimation places the hands in world space. Experiments show improvements in image-space alignment, hand geometry, contact estimation and world-space tracking over the evaluated baselines. The default ViT-L model runs at 65 fps with mesh fitting on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, or 49 fps with parts and contact enabled. The smallest ViT-S model reaches 125 fps without mesh fitting, parts or contact. Code: this https URL.

AI.tldr: FAH is a family of monocular hand estimation models, built on the hand branch of SAM 3D Body, that jointly predict 2D and 3D joints, surface points, MANO or MHR-Hand meshes and world-space hand positions. The default ViT-L model runs at 65 fps with mesh fitting, and the ViT-S model reaches 125 fps without mesh fitting, parts or contact.
AI.motivation: Monocular hand mesh estimators usually predict rig parameters and project them to 2D keypoints, but the authors find that directly predicted 3D joints agree better with 2D predictions, and that fitting a mesh to predicted points reduces mesh error.
AI.method: The models are obtained by fine-tuning and feature distillation from SAM 3D Body's hand branch. They predict corresponding 2D and 3D joints and surface points, fit MANO or MHR-Hand, and optionally estimate anatomical parts and contact without object geometry. Causal refinement reduces acceleration error, and camera estimation places the hands in world space.
AI.result: Experiments show improvements over the evaluated baselines in image-space alignment, hand geometry, contact estimation and world-space tracking. The default ViT-L model runs at 65 fps with mesh fitting on an RTX 4070 Ti SUPER, or 49 fps with parts and contact enabled; the ViT-S model reaches 125 fps without mesh fitting, parts or contact.
AI.conclusion: Predicting 3D joints directly and fitting the mesh to them gives a fast and accurate hand estimator that also supports world-space tracking.

title: Selective Event Evidence and Persistent Temporal Priors for Event-Based Point Tracking
summary: Event cameras enable tracking under fast motion and challenging illumination. However, stable long-term point tracking remains challenging: event activity is sparse and varies with scene content and motion, complicating correspondence, while trajectory estimates can drift over long sequences. Together, these challenges motivate a tracker that selectively uses informative event evidence and retains trajectory constraints across temporal windows. We propose Selective Event Evidence and Persistent Temporal Priors (SEPT), an event-only framework for tracking any point (TAP) over long sequences. SEPT introduces two complementary modules: Task-Adaptive Event Evidence Modulation (TEEM) and Persistent Trajectory Prior (PTP). Using only tracking supervision, TEEM learns a bounded reliability field that weights the event tensor across space, time, and channels before feature extraction. PTP carries geometric information across overlapping windows by marginalizing a fixed local quadratic trajectory model with a Schur complement. Its visibility-aware correction refines overlap coordinates, while a clipped terminal velocity initializes coordinates at newly exposed timestamps. SEPT builds on the ETAP architecture. SEPT is trained exclusively on synthetic EventKubric data and evaluated on five datasets across TAP and feature tracking. Results show that SEPT outperforms the retrained ETAP baseline in average Jaccard for TAP and in feature age and expected feature age for feature tracking; it also surpasses several methods combining event and frame inputs on EC and EDS. The source code is publicly available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: SEPT is an event-only tracker for tracking any point over long sequences, using a learned reliability field over the event tensor and a persistent trajectory prior across overlapping windows. It outperforms a retrained ETAP baseline and surpasses several event-plus-frame methods on EC and EDS.
AI.motivation: Event activity is sparse and depends on scene content and motion, which complicates correspondence, while trajectory estimates drift over long sequences; a tracker must therefore use informative event evidence selectively and keep trajectory constraints across temporal windows.
AI.method: Built on the ETAP architecture, SEPT adds Task-Adaptive Event Evidence Modulation (TEEM), which learns a bounded reliability field that weights the event tensor across space, time and channels before feature extraction, and Persistent Trajectory Prior (PTP), which carries geometric information across windows by marginalizing a fixed local quadratic trajectory model with a Schur complement. A visibility-aware correction refines overlap coordinates, and a clipped terminal velocity initializes newly exposed timestamps. Training uses only tracking supervision on synthetic EventKubric data.
AI.result: SEPT outperforms the retrained ETAP baseline in average Jaccard for TAP and in feature age and expected feature age for feature tracking, across five datasets. It also surpasses several methods that combine event and frame inputs on EC and EDS.
AI.conclusion: Selective use of event evidence and persistent temporal priors improves long-term event-based point tracking, even when trained only on synthetic data.

title: BiGrounder: Bidirectional Training Unlocks the Potential of GUI Grounding
summary: Graphical User Interface (GUI) grounding aims to map natural language instructions to precise operational coordinates, serving as a critical task for autonomous agent interaction. Current approaches formalize GUI grounding as predicting action-coordinate pairs from instructions, with end-to-end training supervised solely by final coordinates. Training datasets typically provide only a small number of descriptions per target coordinate, whereas real-world scenarios involve a much larger set of varied descriptions for the same target, which limits robustness to linguistic variation. While recent GUI grounding paradigms have begun employing reinforcement learning to enhance localization accuracy, models with limited exploratory capability before reinforcement yield constrained improvements even with identical training data during the reinforcement phase. To overcome these limitations, we propose a bidirectional reward paradigm that enables model self-reinforcement. During SFT, bidirectional training equips the model to generate action descriptions from target coordinates. During RL, the model samples semantically consistent instruction variations on-policy and grounds each variation back to its target. A cycle-consistency gate couples semantic quality to grounding success, turning the model's own instruction policy into a source of continually refreshed reinforcement trajectories. Our 4B-parameter model achieves competitive accuracy across five grounding benchmarks in our evaluation, indicating the effectiveness of the proposed training paradigm. this https URL

AI.tldr: BiGrounder trains GUI grounding models with a bidirectional reward paradigm, adding instruction generation from coordinates in SFT and on-policy instruction variations with a cycle-consistency gate in RL. Its 4B-parameter model is reported as competitive on five grounding benchmarks.
AI.motivation: GUI grounding training provides only a few descriptions per target coordinate, which limits robustness to linguistic variation, and RL gains are constrained when the model has little exploratory capability before reinforcement.
AI.method: During SFT the model also learns to generate action descriptions from target coordinates. During RL it samples semantically consistent instruction variations on-policy and grounds each variation back to its target; a cycle-consistency gate couples semantic quality to grounding success, so the model's own instruction policy supplies continually refreshed reinforcement trajectories.
AI.result: The 4B-parameter model achieves competitive accuracy across five grounding benchmarks in the authors' evaluation; the abstract gives no specific numbers or baselines.
AI.conclusion: The bidirectional training paradigm is presented as an effective way for a GUI grounding model to self-reinforce.

title: Rain Beyond Streaks: Cascaded Realistic Rain and Wet Surface Synthesis via Scene Priors
summary: Realistic rain synthesis is a persistent challenge for vision systems operating in adverse weather. Existing methods primarily focus on generating rain streaks, often neglecting consequent surface effects such as reflections and puddles, which are critical for perceptual realism and robustness of downstream vision tasks. We introduce CascadeRS, a rain synthesis framework that leverages depth and segmentation priors to render scene-consistent rain and surface effects. In addition to rain streaks, CascadeRS produces reflections and puddles aligned with scene semantics through a physics-inspired zero-shot, controllable generative pipeline. It produces photorealistic rainy urban scenes, with high perceptual realism, which we validate qualitatively with an extensive user study and quantitatively. We produce the Cityscapes-CascadeRS dataset, to study downstream task performance under real rainy conditions. Our results establish CascadeRS as a scalable and realistic rain-generation framework for evaluating and enhancing the robustness of vision in adverse rainy weather. Code and dataset are available via this https URL

AI.tldr: CascadeRS is a zero-shot, controllable rain synthesis framework that uses depth and segmentation priors to render rain streaks together with reflections and puddles. It also releases the Cityscapes-CascadeRS dataset for studying downstream task performance under real rainy conditions.
AI.motivation: Existing rain synthesis mainly generates streaks and neglects surface effects such as reflections and puddles, which matter for perceptual realism and for the robustness of downstream vision tasks.
AI.method: A physics-inspired, zero-shot, controllable generative pipeline guided by depth and segmentation priors produces rain streaks, reflections and puddles aligned with scene semantics.
AI.result: The authors report photorealistic rainy urban scenes with high perceptual realism, validated qualitatively through an extensive user study and quantitatively; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: CascadeRS is presented as a scalable, realistic rain generator for evaluating and improving the robustness of vision systems in adverse weather.

title: Self-Supervised Diffusion Models for Handwritten Signature Verification via Ruin Reconstruction
summary: Handwritten signature verification (HSV) is a critical biometric technique in legal and forensic authentication, whose efficacy hinges on the discriminability of signature representations. Current HSV methods predominantly adopt supervised learning to enhance representation quality, leaving self-supervised learning largely unexplored. We propose \emph{SigDiffuser}, a diffusion-based self-supervised framework for signature representation and verification. At its core, \emph{SigDiffuser} introduces a novel pretext task termed \emph{Reconstruction from Ruins (RFR)}, which deliberately ``ruins'' signatures through severe crumpling, obliterating their structural integrity and writing styles. A visual encoder is employed to capture crucial handwriting patterns from intact signature regions, guiding the denoiser to reconstruct the ``ruined'' portions and learning meaningful representations. Additionally, we introduce a \emph{pyramidal feature aggregation module (PFAM)} to bridge the visual encoder and denoiser, enhancing representation quality via hierarchical aggregation and modulation. Extensive experiments on multilingual signature datasets demonstrate that \emph{SigDiffuser} significantly outperforms both state-of-the-art SSL methods and HSV models. We further show that increasing the crumpling severity on signatures effectively improves representation quality. Notably, our work demonstrates that extreme destruction, coupled with self-supervised diffusion models, can yield superior signature representation compared to traditional mild deformations, paving new avenues for HSV and other biometric domains. Code will be publicly available.

AI.tldr: SigDiffuser is a diffusion-based self-supervised framework for handwritten signature verification, pretrained with Reconstruction from Ruins, a task that reconstructs heavily crumpled signatures. It outperforms both state-of-the-art SSL methods and HSV models on multilingual signature datasets.
AI.motivation: Handwritten signature verification relies mostly on supervised learning, leaving self-supervised learning largely unexplored, although discriminative signature representations matter for legal and forensic authentication.
AI.method: The pretext task Reconstruction from Ruins (RFR) severely crumples signatures; a visual encoder captures handwriting patterns from the intact regions and guides a denoiser to reconstruct the ruined parts. A pyramidal feature aggregation module (PFAM) bridges the encoder and denoiser through hierarchical aggregation and modulation.
AI.result: SigDiffuser significantly outperforms both state-of-the-art SSL methods and HSV models on multilingual signature datasets, and increasing the crumpling severity improves representation quality.
AI.conclusion: Extreme destruction combined with self-supervised diffusion can yield better signature representations than mild deformations, which may extend to other biometric domains.

title: MV-Sign: Multi-View 3D Motion Integration and Enhanced Text-to-Motion Conditioning for Sign Language Production
comment: Accepted at the IEEE/CVF Winter Conference on Applications of Computer Vision (WACV 2027)
summary: Sign language production (SLP) aims to generate appropriate sign language motion from spoken language text. However, current 3D SLP methods suffer from noisy supervision and weak text conditioning. Specifically, these methods typically rely on pseudo-3D motion data fitted from single-view frontal videos, which introduces severe self-occlusion and loses fine-grained hand details, ultimately degrading downstream production. To overcome these limitations, we propose a comprehensive framework that jointly integrates multi-view 3D motion data and optimizes the text-conditioning pathway. First, we introduce How2Sign-MV3D, a high-fidelity dataset constructed via a novel cross-view curation pipeline that fuses multi-view estimates to resolve occlusions and filter non-signing segments. Second, we design a robust SLP model incorporating a sign-aware spatio-temporal VQ-VAE (ST-VQVAE) for joint body-hand tokenization, a pseudo-gloss adapter, and keyframe-aware retrieval to enhance text-to-motion alignment. Evaluated on the How2Sign benchmark, our framework reduces body and hand DTW-PA-JPE by 32.8% and 20.9% respectively compared to the state-of-the-art. Finally, we release two new high-quality 3D datasets, ASLCitizen-3D and MM-WAuslan-MV3D, alongside SGNify-MV as a multi-view video benchmark to support broader community research.

AI.tldr: MV-Sign improves 3D sign language production by building a multi-view 3D motion dataset and a text-conditioned model with sign-aware VQ-VAE tokenization and keyframe-aware retrieval. On How2Sign it reduces body and hand DTW-PA-JPE by 32.8% and 20.9% relative to the state of the art.
AI.motivation: Current 3D SLP methods use pseudo-3D motion fitted from single-view frontal videos, which introduces severe self-occlusion, loses fine hand detail and weakens text conditioning.
AI.method: The authors build How2Sign-MV3D with a cross-view curation pipeline that fuses multi-view estimates to resolve occlusions and filter non-signing segments. The SLP model uses a sign-aware spatio-temporal VQ-VAE (ST-VQVAE) for joint body-hand tokenization, a pseudo-gloss adapter and keyframe-aware retrieval to enhance text-to-motion alignment.
AI.result: On the How2Sign benchmark the framework reduces body and hand DTW-PA-JPE by 32.8% and 20.9% respectively compared with the state of the art. Two new high-quality 3D datasets (ASLCitizen-3D and MM-WAuslan-MV3D) and a multi-view video benchmark (SGNify-MV) are released.
AI.conclusion: Multi-view 3D supervision together with better text conditioning improves sign language production, and the released datasets support broader community research.

title: CMDiff: Left Atrial Scar Segmentation from 3D LGE MRI Using Conditional Mask Diffusion Model: A Feasibility Study
summary: Late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) cardiac MRI enables non-invasive assessment of left atrial (LA) scar, an imaging marker associated with atrial fibrillation ablation outcome. However, automatic scar segmentation is hindered by low contrast, the thin atrial wall, scarce labels, and extreme class imbalance. Conditional diffusion offers iterative mask generation, but its suitability for sparse 3D LA scar segmentation remains unclear. To address this gap, we propose Conditional Mask Diffusion (CMDiff), which predicts clean masks using a dynamic-encoder-conditioned 3D sinusoidal UNet. We compared CMDiff with a deterministic baseline on identical cases in five-fold cross-validation of 60 scar-labelled public LASCARQS subjects, with 48 training and 12 held-out cases per fold. CMDiff achieved a scar DSC of 0.47 $\pm$ 0.08, HD95 of 12.89 $\pm$ 6.39 mm, and ASD of 1.91 $\pm$ 0.96 mm, compared with deterministic baseline values of 0.51 $\pm$ 0.08, 10.86 $\pm$ 5.39 mm, and 1.58 $\pm$ 1.03 mm, respectively. Under the same implementation, clean-mask prediction performed substantially better than the noise-prediction configuration evaluated in this study. Thus, CMDiff was technically feasible but did not improve segmentation performance: DSC was lower, and both HD95 and ASD were higher. Direct mask diffusion therefore provides an analytical alternative, but not a competitive performance advance for this task. The source code is publicly available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: CMDiff applies conditional mask diffusion to 3D left atrial scar segmentation from LGE MRI as a feasibility study. It does not beat the deterministic baseline: DSC is lower, while HD95 and ASD are higher.
AI.motivation: Automatic LA scar segmentation is hindered by low contrast, a thin atrial wall, scarce labels and extreme class imbalance, and it was unclear whether conditional diffusion suits sparse 3D scar segmentation.
AI.method: CMDiff predicts clean masks with a dynamic-encoder-conditioned 3D sinusoidal UNet. It is compared with a deterministic baseline on identical cases in five-fold cross-validation over 60 scar-labelled LASCARQS subjects (48 training and 12 held-out cases per fold), and clean-mask prediction is compared with a noise-prediction configuration under the same implementation.
AI.result: CMDiff achieved scar DSC 0.47 ± 0.08, HD95 12.89 ± 6.39 mm and ASD 1.91 ± 0.96 mm, versus 0.51 ± 0.08, 10.86 ± 5.39 mm and 1.58 ± 1.03 mm for the deterministic baseline. Clean-mask prediction performed substantially better than noise prediction.
AI.conclusion: Direct mask diffusion is technically feasible and gives an analytical alternative, but it is not a competitive performance advance for this task.

title: STAG-Net: Structure-Aware Attention over Landmark Groups for Lightweight Head Pose Estimation
summary: Head pose estimation is important for human computer interaction and driver monitoring, but many image based methods remain too costly for resource constrained deployment. We propose STAG-Net, a structure-aware attention over landmark groups for lightweight head Pose estimation that estimates head pose from facial landmarks using movement aware selection, spatial clustering, compact DeepSet encoders, self attention, and a global geometry descriptor. We develop variants using FaceMesh and Face Alignment Network landmarks and evaluate them under cross dataset and subject independent protocols on 300W-LP, AFLW2000, and BIWI. STAG-Net achieves the lowest mean absolute error among all compared landmark based methods in every evaluated setting. On BIWI frames with valid detections, the FAN variant also records the lowest overall error among all compared methods, reaching $3.51^\circ$ under cross dataset evaluation and $2.39^\circ$ under subject independent evaluation. The regressors use only 0.012 to 0.043 million parameters and 24.1 to 83.6 thousand FLOPs, about three orders of magnitude fewer FLOPs than FSA-Net. Despite including landmark extraction and regression, the FaceMesh pipeline reaches 322.9 frames per second on a Tesla T4 GPU, nearly twice the 164.5 frames per second of the fastest measured image based baseline, and 111.0 frames per second on CPU. After normalization by dataset size, STAG-Net processes training samples seven to eight times faster than FSA-Net and more than one hundred times faster than HopeNet and TokenHPE, while complete training finishes within 28 minutes. These results show that STAG-Net combines leading landmark based accuracy with substantially lower training and inference cost.

AI.tldr: STAG-Net is a lightweight head pose estimator that regresses pose from facial landmarks using structure-aware attention over landmark groups. It reports the lowest landmark-based MAE in every evaluated setting, with 0.012 to 0.043 million parameters and 322.9 fps on a Tesla T4 for the FaceMesh pipeline.
AI.motivation: Image-based head pose estimators are often too costly for resource-constrained deployment, such as driver monitoring and human-computer interaction.
AI.method: Movement-aware landmark selection, spatial clustering, compact DeepSet encoders, self-attention and a global geometry descriptor regress pose from landmarks. Variants use FaceMesh and Face Alignment Network (FAN) landmarks, evaluated under cross-dataset and subject-independent protocols on 300W-LP, AFLW2000 and BIWI.
AI.result: STAG-Net achieves the lowest mean absolute error among compared landmark-based methods in every evaluated setting. On BIWI frames with valid detections, the FAN variant reaches 3.51 degrees under cross-dataset and 2.39 degrees under subject-independent evaluation. The regressors need 24.1 to 83.6 thousand FLOPs, about three orders of magnitude fewer than FSA-Net; the FaceMesh pipeline runs at 111.0 fps on CPU, and training is seven to eight times faster per sample than FSA-Net, finishing within 28 minutes.
AI.conclusion: STAG-Net combines leading landmark-based accuracy with substantially lower training and inference cost.

title: THG-Omni: Traceable Human-Centric Graph Supervision for Video Reasoning
summary: Omni-modal models can answer questions about video, but their predictions rarely show which participant, event, or interval supports an answer. Moreover, answer-level supervision alone does not teach a model to interpret structured video evidence. To systematically mitigate this issue, we present THG-Omni, a human-centric graph-supervision framework that links Segment Anything Model~3 participant tracks with temporally grounded Qwen3-VL annotations. Candidate semantic claims are checked against the source video and available audio before they are used to construct training questions, while track geometry provides explicit spatial and temporal supervision. The resulting questions teach an omni-modal reasoning model to interpret participant attributes, actions, affect, interactions, and their timing from a structured graph. At inference, THG-Omni uses a predicted graph constructed from the evaluation video. Experiments on IntentBench show consistent improvements over the unadapted backbone across social reasoning, emotion understanding, and deception perception. On NExT-QA, THG-Omni achieves 89.54\% accuracy with the matched graph, compared with 85.10\% without graph input. Further validation experiments show that compact graph input achieves 78.22\% accuracy, compared with 78.02\% using the full graph and 77.58\% without graph input. A complementary diagnostic demonstrates that the predicted graph preserves evidence useful for answering questions even without the source video and audio. Together, these findings show that THG-Omni improves human-centric video reasoning while grounding its evidence in identifiable participants and events. Our codes are available at this https URL

AI.tldr: THG-Omni supervises an omni-modal video reasoning model with traceable human-centric graphs that link SAM 3 participant tracks to temporally grounded Qwen3-VL annotations. It improves over the unadapted backbone on IntentBench and reaches 89.54% on NExT-QA with the matched graph, versus 85.10% without graph input.
AI.motivation: Omni-modal models answer video questions without showing which participant, event or interval supports the answer, and answer-level supervision alone does not teach them to interpret structured video evidence.
AI.method: Candidate semantic claims are checked against the source video and available audio before they are used to construct training questions, and track geometry provides explicit spatial and temporal supervision. At inference the model uses a predicted graph built from the evaluation video.
AI.result: Consistent improvements over the unadapted backbone on IntentBench across social reasoning, emotion understanding and deception perception. On NExT-QA, accuracy is 89.54% with the matched graph and 85.10% without graph input. In further validation experiments, compact graph input achieves 78.22%, versus 78.02% with the full graph and 77.58% without graph input. A predicted graph preserves answer-useful evidence even without the source video and audio.
AI.conclusion: Graph supervision improves human-centric video reasoning while grounding its evidence in identifiable participants and events.

title: OcTreeMamba: Topology-Aware Mamba for 3D Medical Segmentation via Octree Sparsification
comment: 8 pages, 5 figures, accepted by IEEE BIBM 2026
summary: Accurate segmentation of 3D anatomical structures is crucial to medical image analysis. Recently, Mamba-based approaches have achieved promising segmentation performance in capturing long-range dependencies with linear-time computational complexity. However, heuristic selective scanning strategies inherently disrupt the intrinsic spatial hierarchy and increase computational redundancy, ignoring the inherent sparsity of 3D anatomical structures. To this end, we propose OcTreeMamba, a hierarchical framework that incorporates Octree structures into SSM, achieving 3D topology-aware long-range context feature propagation and integration. Specifically, a Structure Learner performs anatomy-adaptive structured sparsification through hierarchical gating and Gumbel-Softmax sampling, enabling differentiable selection of anatomical regions. The selected regions are subsequently organized by a Dynamic Octree Builder into a multi-level topology that preserves their hierarchical connectivity. Based on the constructed Octree, a bidirectional Tree-SSM propagates and integrates contextual features along connectivity-aware leaf--parent--root and root--parent--leaf trajectories. Extensive experiments on four benchmark datasets show that our proposed OcTreeMamba achieves competitive performance \wrt topological continuity and computational efficiency, particularly for recovering the complex structure on vascular datasets. The code is available at this https URL.

AI.tldr: OcTreeMamba is a Mamba-based 3D medical segmentation framework that replaces heuristic scanning with octree-structured sparsification and bidirectional tree-SSM propagation. It reports competitive performance on four benchmarks with better topological continuity, especially on vascular datasets.
AI.motivation: Heuristic selective scanning in Mamba disrupts the intrinsic spatial hierarchy of 3D anatomy, adds computational redundancy and ignores the inherent sparsity of anatomical structures.
AI.method: A Structure Learner performs anatomy-adaptive sparsification through hierarchical gating and Gumbel-Softmax sampling, selecting anatomical regions differentiably. A Dynamic Octree Builder organizes the selected regions into a multi-level topology that preserves their hierarchical connectivity. A bidirectional Tree-SSM propagates and integrates context along leaf-parent-root and root-parent-leaf trajectories.
AI.result: Experiments on four benchmark datasets show competitive performance in topological continuity and computational efficiency, particularly for recovering complex structures in vascular datasets; the abstract gives no specific numbers.
AI.conclusion: Octree-based topology-aware state space modeling is a practical route to efficient 3D medical segmentation that preserves anatomical connectivity.

title: PVDepth: Panoramic Video Depth Estimation via Geometry-Aware Spatiotemporal Adaptation
comment: ICML 2026, Project Page: this https URL
summary: Panoramic video depth estimation is pivotal for applications such as Virtual Reality and World Models. However, advancements in this field are impeded by two primary obstacles: the scarcity of large-scale training data and the unique spatiotemporal challenges of Equirectangular Projection (ERP), which hinder the direct transfer of perspective models. In this paper, we first present PanoCARLA, a large-scale synthetic RGB-D panoramic video dataset, featuring natural motion trajectories and drone-like roaming perspectives. Building on this foundation, we propose PVDepth, an end-to-end framework adapted from perspective video depth models. To tackle ERP-specific geometric distortions and consequent non-linear temporal dynamics, we introduce two core mechanisms: (1) A Progressive Sphere-aware Noise Initialization strategy that anneals the noise distribution from planar to spherical, guiding the model to adapt to non-uniform information density; and (2) A Cube-rectified Temporal Modeling module that incorporates an auxiliary cubemap temporal branch to rectify non-linear temporal dynamics in the ERP domain. Extensive experiments demonstrate that PVDepth achieves superior performance, generating geometrically accurate and temporally consistent depth sequences. Code and data will be released at https:// this http URL.

AI.tldr: PVDepth adapts perspective video depth models to panoramic video, using a new synthetic RGB-D panoramic dataset, PanoCARLA, and two mechanisms for equirectangular projection (ERP). It is reported to produce geometrically accurate and temporally consistent depth sequences.
AI.motivation: Panoramic video depth estimation is hampered by scarce large-scale training data and by the spatiotemporal distortions of ERP, which prevent direct transfer of perspective models.
AI.method: The authors present PanoCARLA, a large-scale synthetic RGB-D panoramic video dataset with natural motion trajectories and drone-like roaming views. PVDepth introduces a Progressive Sphere-aware Noise Initialization that anneals the noise distribution from planar to spherical, and a Cube-rectified Temporal Modeling module with an auxiliary cubemap temporal branch that rectifies non-linear temporal dynamics in the ERP domain.
AI.result: Extensive experiments reportedly show superior performance, with geometrically accurate and temporally consistent depth sequences; the abstract gives no numerical comparisons.
AI.conclusion: Geometry-aware adaptation of perspective depth models, supported by a new panoramic dataset, addresses ERP-specific challenges in panoramic video depth estimation.

title: InnerLogic-Surg: An Open Surgical Foundation Model via Continual Pretraining
summary: Vision foundation models are the backbone of modern surgical image analysis, yet most surgical systems still rely on encoders pretrained on natural images or on specialist models trained from scratch on comparatively small datasets. Pretraining encoders on large amounts of surgery-specific data has the potential to generally enhance the performance of surgical image analysis methods simply by providing stronger backbones. Here we present InnerLogic-Surg, an open family of surgical vision encoders (21M--300M parameters) obtained by continually pretraining a transformer-based image encoder on millions of surgical images curated from 11,965 internet-sourced surgical videos spanning ~2,900 hours and more than fifteen procedure types. Our training recipe inherits DINOv3's pretraining stage to preserve representation ability after surgical adaptation, and additionally applies a learned feature-upsampling module for high-resolution dense prediction at low token cost. Across a benchmark covering workflow, instrument and anatomy recognition, segmentation, detection, and monocular depth, under the same architecture, the largest InnerLogic-Surg model achieves the best linear-probe performance in all 20 surgical tasks. We demonstrate that surgical continual pretraining yields transferable representations that generalize across procedures, anatomical regions, and task types, showing our surgical image encoders as a promising and scalable alternative to the procedure-specific representation learning approaches that have traditionally dominated surgical computer vision.

AI.tldr: InnerLogic-Surg is an open family of surgical vision encoders (21M to 300M parameters) obtained by continually pretraining a transformer image encoder on millions of surgical images. The largest model achieves the best linear-probe performance in all 20 surgical tasks in the benchmark.
AI.motivation: Most surgical systems use encoders pretrained on natural images or specialist models trained from scratch on small datasets, and stronger surgery-specific backbones have the potential to improve many surgical image analysis methods.
AI.method: Continual pretraining of a transformer image encoder on millions of surgical images curated from 11,965 internet-sourced surgical videos (about 2,900 hours, more than fifteen procedure types). The recipe inherits the DINOv3 pretraining stage to preserve representation ability after surgical adaptation and adds a learned feature-upsampling module for high-resolution dense prediction at low token cost.
AI.result: Under the same architecture, the largest InnerLogic-Surg model achieves the best linear-probe performance in all 20 surgical tasks, spanning workflow, instrument and anatomy recognition, segmentation, detection and monocular depth.
